segs.en: Selichot for the Seventeenth of Tammuz
segs.text: סליחות לי"ז בתמוז

segs.en: After the repetition, say the Confession and Nefilat Apayim (Falling on the Face), and then say:
segs.text: <small>אחר החזרה אומרים וידוי ונפילת אפים, ואחר כך אומרים</small>

וָאָרֶץ שָׁפַל רוּמִי, יוֹם דִּמָּה רָשָׁע לְהַכְנִיעִי, מְשׂוֹשׂ לִבִּי שָׁבַת, וְהֻשְׁלַכְתִּי מִבֵּית מַרְגּוֹעִי, אָנוּ וְאָֽבְלוּ פְּתָחַי, יוֹם נֶאֱסַף נְדִיבִי וְשׁוּעִי, לָכֵן אֲקוֹנֵן מִיָּמִים יָמִימָה בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי:

בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי אָֽפְפוּ עָלַי רָעוֹת וַאֲנָחוֹת, בְּשִׁבְעָה־עָשָׂר בּוֹ, בְּאַנְחָתִי יָגַעְתִּי וְלֹא מָצָאתִי מְנוּחוֹת, גָּעֹה גָעִיתִי בִּבְכִי וְעַל כָּל־רֹאשׁ קְרְחוֹת, כִּי בְיוֹם זֶה נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ הַלֻּחוֹת: הַלֻּחוֹת יְצָאוּנִי וְסָֽבְבוּ עָלַי תְּלָאוֹת, וְגָֽבְרָה יַד צָרִי וְזֵרַנִי בְּכָל־פֵּאוֹת, סָב־נָא וְהָגֵן מְיַחֲלֵי קֵץ פְּלָאוֹת, כִּי שֶׁמֶשׁ וּמָגֵן יְהֹוָה צְבָאוֹת:

בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי דִּמִּיתִי עֲלוֹת מִטִּיט הַיָּוֵן וְאֵין מַעֲמִיד, בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בּוֹ הָיִיתִי לְבִזָּה לְמַאֲכָל וּלְהַשְׁמִיד, וְלֹא מָצָאתִי מָנוֹחַ וּמַכְאוֹבִי נֶגְדִּי תָמִיד, כִּי בוֹ בֻּטַּל הַתָּמִיד: הַתָּמִיד יוֹם הוּסַר גָּֽבְרָה יִלְלָתִי כְּיִלְלַת אֶגְלַיִם, וּמִסְפְּדִי גָדַל כְּמִסְפֵּד הֲדַדְרִמּוֹן כִּפְלַיִם, סָב־נָא וְהַחֲיֵה רְדוּמֵֽינוּ, אֵל שׁוֹכֵן שָׁמַיִם, יְחַיֵּֽינוּ מִיּוֹמָיִם:

בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי זַעַם צוּר נָשָׂאתִי וַחֲמָתוֹ בִּי הִבְעִיר, בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בּוֹ חַלְחָלָה אֲחָזַתְנִי וְסַעַר מַסְעִיר, טוֹבוֹת נָשִׁיתִי וַתִּזְנַח מִשָּׁלוֹם נַפְשִׁי בְּתִגְרַת שֵׂעִיר, כִּי בוֹ הָבְקְעָה הָעִיר: הָעִיר יוֹם הָבְקְעָה בְּקוּם תֵּימָן וּמַגְדִּיאֵל, וְאָֽזְלַת יָדִי וְלֹא מָֽצְאָה לָאֵל, סָב־נָא וְהַקְדֵּשׁ פְּלֵיטַת אֲרִיאֵל, הִקְדִּ֙ישׁוּ֙ אֶת־קְד֣וֹשׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְאֶת־אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל:

בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי יוֹם הוֹ הוֹ יוֹם תּוֹכֵחָה וְעֶבְרָה, בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בּוֹ כְּבוֹדִי גָלָה וְתִפְאַרְתִּי הוּסָרָה, לְשִׁבְרִי אֵין כֵּהָה וּמַכָּתִי נַחְלָה וְרוּחִי נִשְׁבָּרָה, כִּי בוֹ שָׂרַף אַפּוֹסְטְמוֹס אֶת־הַתּוֹרָה: הַתּוֹרָה יוֹם נִשְׂרְפָה חֻדְּשׁוּ עָלַי יְגוֹנַי, וְשָֽׁבְתוּ מֵעִיר קֹדֶשׁ יְשִׁישַׁי וּזְקֵנַי, סָב־נָא וְחֹן בְּעֻזְּךָ עֲדַת אֱמוּנַי, ר֥וּחַ דַּ֖עַת וְיִרְאַ֥ת יְהֹוָֽה׃

בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי מְעֻוָּתִי מָדַד זָר בְּסַאסְּאָה וּבָהּ כָּֽל, בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בּוֹ נָוִי הֵשַׁם זָר וְאֶת־יַעֲקֹב אָכַל, סְפוֹת שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה בְּיוֹם זֶה מַמְרוּר אוֹכַל, כִּי בוֹ הָעֳמָד צֶלֶם בַּהֵיכָל: יוֹם הָעֳמָד פֶּסֶל קִנְאָה וְתוֹעֵבָה, וּבוֹ חֻבְּלָה רוּחִי וְתוֹחַלְתִּי נִכְזְבָה, סָב־נָא וְרַפֵּא מְשׁוּבַת עַמְּךָ וְתֹאהֲבֵם נְדָבָה, הֲשִׁיבֵ֨נוּ יְהֹוָ֤ה ׀ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה:

עַל יְדֵי רַחֲמֶיךָ הָרַבִּים סְלַח לָנוּ אָבִֽינוּ, כִּי בְרוֹב אִוַּלְתֵּנוּ שָׁגִֽינוּ: מְחֹל לָנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ, כִּי רַבּוּ עֲוֹנֵֽינוּ: אֵל אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם אַתָּה, וְדֶרֶךְ תְּשׁוּבָה לָנוּ הוֹרֵיתָ: גְּדֻלַּת רַחֲמֶיךָ וַחֲסָדֶיךָ, תִּזְכֹּר הַיּוֹם לְזֶרַע יְדִידֶיךָ: תֵּפֶן אֵלֵֽינוּ בְּרַחֲמִים, כִּי אַתָּה הוּא בַּעַל הָרַחֲמִים: בְּתַחֲנוּן וּבִתְפִלָּה נְקַדֵּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוֹדַעְתָּ לֶעָנָו מִקֶּדֶם: וּמֵחֲרוֹן אַפְּךָ תָּשׁוּב, כְּמוֹ בְּתוֹרָֽתְךָ כָּתוּב: וּבְצֵל כְּנָפֶיךָ נֶחֱסֶה וְנִתְלוֹנָן, כְּיוֹם וַיֵּרֶד יְהֹוָה בֶּעָנָן: תַּעֲבוֹר עַל פֶּשַׁע וְתִמְחֹל אָשָׁם, כְּיוֹם וַיִּתְיַצֵּב עִמּוֹ שָׁם: תַּאֲזִין שֶׁוַע וְתַּקְשִׁיב בְּרָצוֹן מַאֲמַר, כְּיוֹם וַיִּקְרָא בְשֵׁם, יְהֹוָה: וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר:

וַיַּעֲבֹ֨ר יְהֹוָ֥ה ׀ עַל־פָּנָיו֮ וַיִּקְרָא֒ יְהֹוָ֣ה ׀ יְהֹוָ֔ה אֵ֥ל רַח֖וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַפַּ֖יִם וְרַב־חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃ נֹצֵ֥ר‏ חֶ֙סֶד֙ לָאֲלָפִ֔ים נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֛ן וָפֶ֖שַׁע וְחַטָּאָ֑ה וְנַקֵּה֙:

segs.en: According to the order of Aleph-Bet
segs.text: <small>על סדר א"ב</small>

אֲזַי בְּבָגְדִי, אִמְרֵי דָר מְעוֹנִי, בְּהִשְׂתָּרֵג עֲוֹנִי, הִכְבִּיד עֻלִי מוֹנִי, גָּבַר עָלַי זָר בְּמַהֲלֹם לְהַלְּמֵנִי, אַפּוֹ טָרַף וַיִּשְׂטְמֵנִי: דְּרָכָיו זָנַחְתִּי אֲשֶׁר לִי הוֹרָה, הֵן עַל כֵּן הֵעִיר בִּי אַף וְזַעַם וְעֶבְרָה, זַעְמוֹ בִּי הֵרִיק וְחִצָּיו בִּי יָרָה, וַיְקִימֵנִי לוֹ לְמַטָּרָה: חָֽלְפוּ עָלַי בְּיוֹם זֶה חָמֵשׁ תְּלָאוֹת, טָֽרְפוּ חַיָּתִי וַיְשִׂימוּנִי לְמַשּׁוּאוֹת, יָֽגְעָה נַפְשִׁי יָגוֹעַ וְהַלְאוֹת, נַעֲוֵיתִי מִשְּׁמֹעַ, נִבְהַלְתִּי מֵרְאוֹת: כָּל־אֵלֶּה בְּזָכְרִי יְעוֹרְרוּנִי אֲנָחוֹת, לֶהָבָה הֱשִׂיקַתְנִי מְלַהֶטֶת כֶּסֶל וְטוּחוֹת, מִסְפֵּד מַר אַגְדִּיל וְאַרְחִיק שְׂמָחוֹת, כִּי בְיוֹם זֶה נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ הַלּוּחוֹת: נוֹעַד עָלַי זָר וַהֲמוֹנָיו הִצְמִיד, סַבּוּנִי כַמַּיִם וְטָבַעְתִּי וְאֵין מַעֲמִיד, עַל כֵּן אֲיֵלִיל בְּמוֹ פִי, וְנֶהִי אַתְמִיד, כִּי בְיוֹם זֶה בֻּטַּל הַתָּמִיד: פּוֹשְׁחַי הָמוּ כַּהֲמוֹת זֶרֶם מִיכַל, צָֽמְתוּ בַבּוֹר חַיַּי וַיִּתְּנוּנִי לְמַאֲכָל, קָרָא עָלַי מוֹעֵד וַהֲמוֹנַי שָׁכֹל שִׁכַּל, כִּי בְּיוֹם זֶה הָעֳמָד צֶלֶם בָּהֵיכָל: רַבָּתִי עָם, זָר הֵצַר וּפְתָחֶיהָ פֶּתַח הֶעֱרָה, שָׁת גַּפְנִי לְשַׁמָּה בְּיוֹם זָעַם וְעֶבְרָה, תַּאֲוָתוֹ רָאָה זָר וְיָדוֹ בְּעֹז גָּֽברָה, כִּי בְיוֹם זֶה שָׂרַף אַפּוֹסְטְמוֹס אֶת־הַתּוֹרָה:

חָֽרְקוּ שֵׁן רְשָׁעִים בְּיוֹם אַף יְהֹוָה בִּי הֵעִיר, לֹא חָמַל זָר וְעִקֵּשׁ עַל יָשִׁישׁ וְצָעִיר, אַפּוֹ בִּי חָרָה וּרְשָׁפָּיו בִּי הִבְעִיר, כִּי בְיוֹם זֶה הָבְקְעָה הָעִיר: רַחֵם יְהֹוָה וְדַבֵּר עַל לֵב עֲגוּמִים, בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר לַחֹדֶשׁ יוֹשְׁבִים מִשְׁתּוֹמְמִים, יָהּ גַּלְגֵּל עֲלֵיהֶם הֲמוֹן רַחֲמֶיךָ מִמְּרוֹמִים, אֵל מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רַחֲמִים:

שְׁעֵה נֶאְסָר, אֲשֶׁר נִמְסַר, בְּיַד בָּבֶל וְשַׂר הָעִיר: לְךָ יֶהֱמֶה, זֶה כַמֶּה, וְיִתְחַנֵּן כְּבֶן צָעִיר: מוּלְךָ צוּר, בְּלֵב עָצוּר, הֶמְיַת מֵעָיו יַסְעִיר: יוֹם גָּבַר הָאוֹיֵב וַתִּבָּקַע הָעִיר: לְזֹאת אִכַּף, וְאֶסְפֹּק כַּף, בְּיוֹם חָמֵשׁ קְרָאוּנִי: וְעַל רֶגֶל, הָעֵגֶל, הַלּוּחוֹת יְצָאוּנִי: וְלָכַד זָר, הַמִּבְצָר, וּבְמַסְגֵּר הֱבִיאָנִי: וְגַם הִשְׁמִיד, הַתָּמִיד, וּמֵעֲשׂוֹתוֹ כְּלָאָנִי: וְהוּשָׂם אֱלִיל, בְּהֵיכָל כָּלִיל, וְדָֽתְךָ זָר בָּאֵשׁ הִבְעִיר: מְאֹד אֶתְחַל, וָאֶתְחַלְחַל, בְּיוֹם שַׁדַּי חֲשָׂפַנִי: וְהַשְּׁפִיפוֹן, מִצָּפוֹן, כְּשִׁבּוֹלֶת שְׁטָפַנִי: וְנָהַג שְׁבִי, אֶרֶץ צְבִי, וְגַם כַּדּוּר צְנָפַנִי: יוֹם חָשַׁךְ, מְאוֹר שֵׁשַׁךְ, לְיַד פָּרַס דְּחָפַנִי: אֲכָלַנִי, הֲמָמַנִי, וְקִינָה עֲלֵי זֹאת אָעִיר: הֲלָעַד בִּי, מִשְׂגַּבִּי, הֲלָעַד אַפְּךָ יֶעְשַׁן: גְּדוֹר פִּרְצִי, בְּבֶן פַּרְצִי, וּמֵחֶדֶק לְקֹט שׁוֹשָׁן: עַיִן פְּקַח, תְּפִלָּתִי קַח, כְּמוֹ חֵלֶב הַמְּדֻשָׁן: בְּנֵה בֵית זְבוּל, וְהָשֵׁב גְּבוּל, הַכַּרְמֶל וְהַבָּשָׁן: שְׁפֹט אִלֵּם, וְאָז יְשַׁלֵּם, הַמַּבְעֶה וְהַמַּבְעִיר:

אֱלֹהֵי יְשׁוּעָתֵנוּ, שְׁעֵה שַׁוְעָתֵנוּ, וּרְאֵה שׁוֹמְמוֹתֵֽינוּ, וְאֹרֶךְ גָּלוּתֵנוּ, מִדֵּי שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה, בְּזָכְרֵנוּ עֱנוּתֵנוּ, בְּיוֹם חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים, אֵרְעוּ אֶת־אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ: נָא אֱלֹהֵי הָרוּחוֹת, וּבוֹחֵן סִתְרֵי טוּחוֹת, שְׁעֵה שֵׂיוֹת נִדָּחוֹת, נְפוּצוֹת בְּאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת, מִדֵּי שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה בִּזְמַן זֶה נֶאֱנָחוֹת, בְּיוֹם עֵקֶב מַדּוּחוֹת, נִשְׁתַּבְּרוּ הַלּוּחוֹת, וּבוֹ כָּל־יְמֵי שְׁנוֹתֵֽינוּ, נְמָרֵר עַל יְגוֹנֵנוּ: דְּלֵה מִטִּיט הַיָּוֵן, טְבוּעִים בּוֹ וְאֵין מַעֲמִיד, עֵדֶר תַּתָּה לְמַאֲכָל, לְבִזָּה וּלְהַשְׁמִיד, מִדֵּי שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה, בְּיוֹם זֶה עֶצֶב מַצְמִיד, יוֹם בּוֹ יַד זָר הֶאֱמִיר, וּבוֹ בֻּטַּל הַתָּמִיד, עַל רֹב עֲוֹנוֹתֵֽינוּ, וְעֹצֶם חַטֹּאתֵֽינוּ: יָהּ אֲשֶׁר הַכֹּל יוּכַל, פְּדֵה מִשּׁכוֹל שָׁכַל, מִיַּד עִקֵּשׁ וְסָכָל, וּשְׁאַר יַעֲקֹב אָכַל, מִדֵּי שָׁנָה בְּשָׁנָה, בְּיוֹם זֶה מַמְרֹר אוֹכַל, בְּהַעֲמִיד זָר לְמוּלִי, בּוֹ צֶלֶם בַּהֵיכָל, עַל כָּל־קוֹרוֹתֵֽינוּ יִזְּלוּ דִמְעוֹתֵֽינוּ: שִׁבְרֵנוּ מַה־נּוֹרָא, כִּי סַרְנוּ מִמּוֹרָא, נָאוֹר עֹטֶה אוֹרָה, גְּמוּלִי לַכָֹּל הוֹרָה, מִדֵּי שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה, נֶהִי בְּיוֹם זֶה אֶחְקוֹרָה, יַעַן כִּי בוֹ שָׂרַף אַפּוֹסְטְמוֹס אֶת־הַתּוֹרָה, לְזֹאת נִשְׁכְּבָה בְּבָשְׁתֵּנוּ, לְשׁוֹד בֵּית תִּפְאַרְתֵּנוּ: רַחוּם יְכַפֵּר עָוֹן, וְכָל־חֲמָתוֹ לֹא יָעִיר, פְּדֵה חִישׁ מִידֵי שָׂעִיר, פְּזוּרֵי הַצֹּאן וְצָעִיר, מִדֵּי שָׁנָה בְשָׁנָה, בְּיוֹם זֶה הֶמְיַת מֵעָיו יַסְעִיר, יוֹם גָּֽבְרוּ הַזָּרִים וַתִּבָּקַע הָעִיר, כִּי הָיִֽינוּ לְלַעַג וָקֶלֶס לִסְבִיבוֹתֵֽינוּ: רַחֲמָן בְּרַחֲמִים שׁוּבָה, אֶל צִיּוֹן הָעֲלוּבָה, וְחִישׁ נָא לְאִשָּׁה עֲצוּבָה, נֶחָמָה הַכְּתוּבָה, וְאָז שִׁירָה נָנוּבָה, בִּבְנוֹתְךָ הַחֲרֵבָה, בְּקִבּוּץ נְפוּצוֹתֵֽינוּ, וּבְשׁוּבְךָ אֶת שְׁבוּתֵנוּ:

אֵל מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רַחֲמִים וּמִתְנַהֵג בַּחֲסִידוּת, מוֹחֵל עֲוֹנוֹת עַמּוֹ, מַעֲבִיר רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן. מַרְבֶּה מְחִילָה לַחַטָּאִים, וּסְלִיחָה לַפּוֹשְׁעִים. עֹשֶׂה צְדָקוֹת עִם כָּל־בָּשָׂר וְרוּחַ, לֹא כְרָעָתָם לָהֶם גּוֹמֵל. אֵל הוֹרֵתָנוּ לוֹמַר מִדּוֹת שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה, זְכֹר לָנוּ הַיּוֹם בְּרִית שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוֹדַעְתָּ לֶעָנָו מִקֶּדֶם, וְכֵן כָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתָךְ: וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהֹוָה֙ בֶּֽעָנָ֔ן וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב עִמּ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְשֵׁ֖ם יְהֹוָֽה׃ וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר:

וַיַּעֲבֹ֨ר יְהֹוָ֥ה ׀ עַל־פָּנָיו֮ וַיִּקְרָא֒ יְהֹוָ֣ה ׀ יְהֹוָ֔ה אֵ֥ל רַח֖וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַפַּ֖יִם וְרַב־חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃ נֹצֵ֥ר‏ חֶ֙סֶד֙ לָאֲלָפִ֔ים נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֛ן וָפֶ֖שַׁע וְחַטָּאָ֑ה וְנַקֵּה֙׃

segs.en: According to the order of Aleph-Bet
segs.text: <small>על סדר א"ב</small>

אַנְשֵׁי אֱמוּנָה אָבָדוּ, בָּאִים בְּכֹחַ מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם: גִּבּוֹרִים לַעֲמֹד בַּפֶּרֶץ, דּוֹחִים אֶת־הַגְּזֵרוֹת: הָיוּ לָנוּ לְחוֹמָה, וּלְמַחְסֶה בְּיוֹם זָעַם: זוֹעֲכִים אַף בְּלַחֲשָׁם, חֵמָה עָֽצְרוּ בְּשַׁוְּעָם: טֶרֶם קְרָאוּךָ עֲנִיתָם, יוֹדְעִים לַעֲתֹר וּלְרַצּוֹת: כְּאָב רִחַמְתָּ לְמַעֲנָם, לֹא הֱשִׁיבוֹתָ פְנֵיהֶם רֵיקָם: מֵרֹב עֲוֹנֵֽינוּ אֲבַדְנוּם, נֶאֶסְפוּ מֶנּוּ בַּחֲטָאֵֽינוּ: סָעוּ הֵמָּה לִמְנוּחוֹת, עָֽזְבוּ אוֹתָנוּ לַאֲנָחוֹת: פַּסּוּ גוֹדְרֵי גָדֵר, צֻמְּתוּ מְשִׁיבֵי חֵמָה: קָמִים בַּפֶּרֶץ אַיִן, רְאוּיִים לְרַצּוֹתְךָ אָפֵסוּ: שׁוֹטַטְנוּ בְּאַרְבַּע פִּנּוֹת, תְּרוּפָה לֹא מָצָאנוּ: שַׁבְנוּ אֵלֶיךָ בְּבֹשֶׁת פָּנֵֽינוּ, לְשַׁחֲרָךְ אֵל בְּעֵת צָרוֹתֵֽינוּ:

אֵל מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רַחֲמִים וּמִתְנַהֵג בַּחֲסִידוּת, מוֹחֵל עֲוֹנוֹת עַמּוֹ, מַעֲבִיר רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן. מַרְבֶּה מְחִילָה לַחַטָּאִים, וּסְלִיחָה לַפּוֹשְׁעִים. עֹשֶׂה צְדָקוֹת עִם כָּל־בָּשָׂר וְרוּחַ, לֹא כְרָעָתָם לָהֶם גּוֹמֵל. אֵל הוֹרֵתָנוּ לוֹמַר מִדּוֹת שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה, זְכֹר לָנוּ הַיּוֹם בְּרִית שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוֹדַעְתָּ לֶעָנָו מִקֶּדֶם, וְכֵן כָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתָךְ: וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהֹוָה֙ בֶּֽעָנָ֔ן וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב עִמּ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְשֵׁ֖ם יְהֹוָֽה׃ וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר:

וַיַּעֲבֹ֨ר יְהֹוָ֥ה ׀ עַל־פָּנָיו֮ וַיִּקְרָא֒ יְהֹוָ֣ה ׀ יְהֹוָ֔ה אֵ֥ל רַח֖וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַפַּ֖יִם וְרַב־חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃ נֹצֵ֥ר‏ חֶ֙סֶד֙ לָאֲלָפִ֔ים נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֛ן וָפֶ֖שַׁע וְחַטָּאָ֑ה וְנַקֵּה֙׃

segs.en: According to the order of Tesh-Rak
segs.text: <small>על סדר תשר"ק</small>

תָּמַהְנוּ מֵרָעוֹת, תָּשַׁשׁ כֹּחֵנוּ מִצָּרוֹת. שַׁחְנוּ עַד לִמְאֹד, שָׁפַלְנוּ עַד עָפָר. רַחוּם כָּךְ הִיא מִדָּתֵנוּ, קְשֵׁי עֹרֶף וּמַמְרִים אֲנַחְנוּ. צָעַקְנוּ בְּפִֽינוּ חָטָאנוּ, פְּתַלְתּוֹל וְעִקֵּשׁ לִבֵּנוּ. עֶלְיוֹן רַחֲמֶיךָ מֵעוֹלָם, סְלִיחָה עִמְּךָ הִיא. נִחָם עַל הָרָעָה, מַטֵּה כְלַפֵּי חֶסֶד. לֹא תִתְעַלַּם בְּעִתּוֹת כָּאֵל, כִּי בְצָרָה גְדוֹלָה אֲנָחְנוּ. יִוָּדַע לְעֵינֵי הַכֹּל, טוּבְךָ וְחַסְדְּךָ עִמָּנוּ. חֲתֹם פֶּה־שָׂטָן, וְאַל יַשְׂטִין עָלֵֽינוּ, זְעֹם בּוֹ וְיִדֹּם. וְיַעֲמֹד מֵלִיץ טוֹב לְצַדְּקֵנוּ, הוּא יַגִּיד יָשְׁרֵנוּ. דְּרָכֶיךָ רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן גִּלִּיתָ לְנֶאֱמַן בָּיִת. בְּבַקְשׁוֹ אָז מִלְּפָנֶיךָ, אֱמוּנָֽתְךָ הוֹדַעְתָּ לּוֹ:

אֵל מֶלֶךְ יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא רַחֲמִים וּמִתְנַהֵג בַּחֲסִידוּת, מוֹחֵל עֲוֹנוֹת עַמּוֹ, מַעֲבִיר רִאשׁוֹן רִאשׁוֹן. מַרְבֶּה מְחִילָה לַחַטָּאִים, וּסְלִיחָה לַפּוֹשְׁעִים. עֹשֶׂה צְדָקוֹת עִם כָּל־בָּשָׂר וְרוּחַ, לֹא כְרָעָתָם לָהֶם גּוֹמֵל. אֵל הוֹרֵתָנוּ לוֹמַר מִדּוֹת שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה, זְכֹר לָנוּ הַיּוֹם בְּרִית שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהוֹדַעְתָּ לֶעָנָו מִקֶּדֶם, וְכֵן כָּתוּב בְּתוֹרָתָךְ: וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהֹוָה֙ בֶּֽעָנָ֔ן וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב עִמּ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְשֵׁ֖ם יְהֹוָֽה׃ וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר:

וַיַּעֲבֹ֨ר יְהֹוָ֥ה ׀ עַל־פָּנָיו֮ וַיִּקְרָא֒ יְהֹוָ֣ה ׀ יְהֹוָ֔ה אֵ֥ל רַח֖וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַפַּ֖יִם וְרַב־חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃ נֹצֵ֥ר‏ חֶ֙סֶד֙ לָאֲלָפִ֔ים נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֛ן וָפֶ֖שַׁע וְחַטָּאָ֑ה וְנַקֵּה֙׃

וּכְשֶׁחָֽטְאוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּמִּדְבָּר, עָמַד מֹשֶׁה בִּתְפִלָּה לְפָנֶיךָ, וּבִקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים עַל עַמְּךָ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְכָךְ אָמַר בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ: סְלַֽח־נָ֗א לַעֲוֺ֛ן הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה כְּגֹ֣דֶל חַסְדֶּ֑ךָ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֤ר נָשָׂ֙אתָה֙ לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם וְעַד־הֵֽנָּה׃ אַף אַתָּה הֱשִׁיבוֹתָ לוֹ כְּדַרְכֵי טוּבְךָ בִּשַּׂרְתּוֹ וַחֲנַנְתּוֹ וְאָמַרְתָּ לוֹ: סָלַחְתִּי כִּדְבָרֶךָ:

דָּנִיֵּאל אִישׁ חֲמוּדוֹת אָמַר לְפָנֶיךָ: הַטֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהַ֥י ׀ אׇזְנְךָ֮ וּֽשְׁמָע֒ פקחה [פְּקַ֣ח] עֵינֶ֗יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ שֹֽׁמְמֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהָעִ֕יר אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּ֣י ׀ לֹ֣א עַל־צִדְקֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ מַפִּילִ֤ים תַּחֲנוּנֵ֙ינוּ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֖י עַל־רַחֲמֶ֥יךָ הָרַבִּֽים׃ אֲדֹנָ֤י ׀ שְׁמָ֙עָה֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י ׀ סְלָ֔חָה אֲדֹנָ֛י הַֽקְשִׁ֥יבָה וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה אַל־תְּאַחַ֑ר לְמַֽעַנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּֽי־שִׁמְךָ֣ נִקְרָ֔א עַל־עִירְךָ֖ וְעַל־עַמֶּֽךָ׃ וְלִירוּשָׁלַיִם עִירָךְ אָמַרְתָּ לָהּ: הִנְנִי֙ נִשְׁפָּ֣ט אוֹתָ֔ךְ עַל־אׇמְרֵ֖ךְ לֹ֥א חָטָֽאתִי׃ אֲנַחְנוּ בּוֹשְׁנוּ בְּמַעֲשֵֽׂינוּ וְנִכְלַמְנוּ בַּעֲוֹנוֹתֵֽינוּ, אֵין לָנוּ פֶּה לְהָשִׁיב וְלֹא מֵצַח לְהָרִים רֹאשׁ:

segs.en: According to the order of Aleph-Tet, Bet-Shin
segs.text: <small>על סדר א"ת ב"ש</small>

אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ אַל תַּעַשׂ עִמָּנוּ כָּלָה, תֹּאחֵז יָֽדְךָ בַּמִּשְׁפָּט. בְּבֹא תוֹכֵחָה נֶגְדֶּךָ, שְׁמֵנוּ מִסִּפְרְךָ אַל תֶּמַח. גִּשְׁתְּךָ לַחֲקֹר מוּסָר, רַחֲמֶיךָ יְקַדְּמוּ רָגְזֶךָ. דַּלּוּת מַעֲשִׂים בְּשׁוּרֶךָ, קָרֵב צֶדֶק מֵאֵלֶיךָ. הוֹרֵנוּ בְּזַעֲקֵנוּ לָךְ, צַו יְשׁוּעָתֵנוּ בְּמַפְגִּיעַ. וְתָשִׁיב שְׁבוּת אָהֳלֵי תָם, פְּתָחָיו רְאֵה כִּי שָׁמֵמוּ. זְכֹר נָאַמְתָּ, עֵדוּת לֹא תִשָּׁכַח מִפִּי זַרְעוֹ. חוֹתָם תְּעוּדָה תַּתִּיר, סוֹדְךָ שִׂים בְּלִמּוּדֶיךָ. טַבּוּר אַגַּן הַסַּהַר, נָא אַל יֶחְסַר הַמָּזֶג. יָהּ דַּע אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר יְדָעוּךָ, מַגֵּר אֶת־הַגּוֹיִם אֲשֶׁר לֹא יְדָעוּךָ. כִּי תָשִׁיב לְבִצָּרוֹן, לְכוּדִים אֲסִירֵי הַתִּקְוָה:

אָשַׁמְנוּ מִכָּל־עָם, בֹּשְׁנוּ מִכָּל־גּוֹי. גָּלָה מִמֶּנּוּ מָשׂוֹשׂ, דָּוֶה לִבֵּנוּ בַּחֲטָאֵֽינוּ. הָחְבַּל אֶוְיֵֽינוּ, וְנִפְרָע פְּאֵרֵנוּ. זְבוּל מִקְדָּשֵׁנוּ, חָרֵב בַּעֲוֹנֵֽינוּ. טִירָתֵנוּ הָֽיְתָה לְשַׁמָּה, יְפִי אַדְמָתֵנוּ לְזָרִים, כֹּחֵנוּ לְנָכְרִים. לְעֵינֵינוּ עָֽשְׁקוּ עֲמָלֵנוּ, מְמֻשָּׁךְ וּמוֹרָט מִמֶּנּוּ. נָֽתְנוּ עֻלָּם עָלֵֽינוּ, סָבַלְנוּ עַל שִׁכְמֵנוּ. עֲבָדִים מָֽשְׁלוּ בָנוּ, פּוֹרֵק אֵין מִיָּדָם. צָרוֹת רַבּוֹת סְבָבוּנוּ, קְרָאנוּךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ. רָחַקְתָּ מִמֶּנּוּ בַּעֲוֹנֵֽינוּ, שַׁבְנוּ מֵאַחֲרֶיךָ, תָּעִֽינוּ כַּצֹּאן וְאָבָֽדְנוּ. וַעֲדַיִן לֹא שַׁבְנוּ מִתְּעִיָּתֵנוּ, וְהֵיאַךְ נָעִיז פָּנֵֽינוּ, וְנַקְשֶׁה עָרְפֵּנוּ, לוֹמַר לְפָנֶיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ צַדִּיקִים אֲנַחְנוּ וְלֹא־חָטָאנוּ:

עֶזְרָא הַסּוֹפֵר אָמַר לְפָנֶיךָ: אֱלֹהַי֙ בֹּ֣שְׁתִּי וְנִכְלַ֔מְתִּי לְהָרִ֧ים אֱלֹהַ֛י פָּנַ֖י אֵלֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י עֲוֺנֹתֵ֤ינוּ רָבוּ֙ לְמַ֣עְלָה רֹּ֔אשׁ וְאַשְׁמָתֵ֥נוּ גָדְלָ֖ה עַ֥ד לַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃ וְאַתָּה אֱלוֹהַּ סְלִיחוֹת, חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם, אֶרֶךְ־אַפַּיִם וְרַב־חֶסֶד, וְלֹא עֲזַבְתָּם. אַל תַּעַזְבֵנוּ אָבִֽינוּ, אַל תִּטְּשֵׁנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ, וְאַל תִּשְׁכָּחֵנוּ יוֹצְרֵנוּ, וְאַל תַּעַשׂ עִמָּנוּ כָלָה בְּגָלוּתֵנוּ, וְקַיֵּם לָנוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ אֶת־הַדָּבָר שֶׁהִבְטַחְתָּנוּ, עַל יְדֵי יִרְמְיָה חוֹזָךְ, כָּאָמוּר: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵם֩ וּבָעֵ֨ת הַהִ֜יא נְאֻם־יְהֹוָ֗ה יְבֻקַּ֞שׁ אֶת־עֲוֺ֤ן יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאֵינֶ֔נּוּ וְאֶת־חַטֹּ֥את יְהוּדָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תִמָּצֶ֑אינָה כִּ֥י אֶסְלַ֖ח לַאֲשֶׁ֥ר אַשְׁאִֽיר׃ וְאַל יְעַכֵּב לְפָנֶיךָ כָּל־חֵטְא וְעוֹן אֶת תְּפִלָּתֵנוּ, וּמְחוֹל וּסְלַח לְכָל־עֲוֹנוֹתֵֽינוּ, כִּי אֵל טוֹב וְסַלָּח אָתָּה:

מַה־נֹּאמַר לְפָנֶיךָ יוֹשֵׁב מָרוֹם, וּמַה נְּסַפֵּר לְפָנֶיךָ שׁוֹכֵן שְׁחָקִים, הֲלֹא הַנִּסְתָּרוֹת וְהַנִּגְלוֹת אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ, אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ רָזֵי עוֹלָם, וְתַעֲלוּמוֹת סִתְרֵי כָל־חָי, אַתָּה חוֹפֵשׂ כָּל־חַדְרֵי בָטֶן, רֹאֶה כלָיוֹת וָלֵב. אֵין דָּבָר נֶעְלָם מִמָּךְ, וְאֵין נִסְתָּר מִנֶּגֶד עֵינֶיךָ:

יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ, שֶׁתִּמְחֹל לָנוּ אֶת־כָּל־חַטֹּאתֵינוּ, וּתְכַפֵּר לָנוּ אֶת־כָּל־עֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ, וְתִמְחֹל וְתִסְלַח לְכָל־פְּשָׁעֵינוּ, וְסָלַחְתָּ לַעֲוֹנֵנוּ וּלְחַטָּאתֵנוּ וּנְחַלְתָּנוּ: סְלַח לָנוּ אָבִינוּ כִּי חָטָאנוּ, מְחֹל לָנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ כִּי פָשָֽׁעְנוּ: כִּי אַתָּה אֲדֹנָי, טוֹב וְסַלָּח, וְרַב־חֶסֶד לְכָל־קֹרְאֶיךָ: לְמַֽעַן־שִׁמְךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֑ה וְֽסָלַחְתָּ֥ לַ֝עֲוֺנִ֗י כִּ֣י רַב־הֽוּא׃ לְמַעַן־שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהֹוָ֣ה תְּחַיֵּ֑נִי בְּצִדְקָתְךָ֓ ׀ תּוֹצִ֖יא מִצָּרָ֣ה נַפְשִֽׁי׃ יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֣וֹת עִמָּ֑נוּ מִשְׂגָּֽב־לָ֨נוּ אֱלֹהֵ֖י יַֽעֲקֹ֣ב סֶֽלָה׃ יְהֹוָ֥ה צְבָא֑וֹת אַֽשְׁרֵ֥י אָ֝דָ֗ם בֹּטֵ֥חַ בָּֽךְ׃ יְהֹוָ֥ה הוֹשִׁ֑יעָה הַ֝מֶּ֗לֶךְ יַעֲנֵ֥נוּ בְיוֹם־קׇרְאֵֽנוּ׃ הֲשִׁיבֵ֨נוּ יְהֹוָ֤ה ׀ אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ ונשוב [וְֽנָשׁ֔וּבָה] חַדֵּ֥שׁ יָמֵ֖ינוּ כְּקֶֽדֶם׃

וְה֤וּא רַח֨וּם ׀ יְכַפֵּ֥ר עָוֺן֮ וְֽלֹא־יַֽ֫שְׁחִ֥ית וְ֭הִרְבָּה לְהָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ וְלֹא־יָ֝עִ֗יר כׇּל־חֲמָתֽוֹ׃ אַתָּ֤ה יְהֹוָ֗ה לֹֽא־תִכְלָ֣א רַחֲמֶ֣יךָ מִמֶּ֑נִּי חַסְדְּךָ֥ וַ֝אֲמִתְּךָ֗ תָּמִ֥יד יִצְּרֽוּנִי׃ הוֹשִׁיעֵ֨נוּ ׀ יְהֹ֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְקַבְּצֵנוּ֮ מִֽן־הַגּ֫וֹיִ֥ם לְ֭הֹדוֹת לְשֵׁ֣ם קׇדְשֶׁ֑ךָ לְ֝הִשְׁתַּבֵּ֗חַ בִּתְהִלָּתֶֽךָ: אִם־עֲוֺנ֥וֹת תִּשְׁמׇר־יָ֑הּ אֲ֝דֹנָ֗י מִ֣י יַעֲמֹֽד׃ כִּֽי־עִמְּךָ֥ הַסְּלִיחָ֑ה לְ֝מַ֗עַן תִּוָּרֵֽא׃ לֹ֣א כַ֭חֲטָאֵינוּ עָ֣שָׂה לָ֑נוּ וְלֹ֥א כַ֝עֲוֺנֹתֵ֗ינוּ גָּמַ֥ל עָלֵֽינוּ׃ אִם־עֲוֺנֵ֙ינוּ֙ עָ֣נוּ בָ֔נוּ יְהֹוָ֕ה עֲשֵׂ֖ה לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמֶ֑ךָ׃ זְכֹר־רַחֲמֶ֣יךָ יְ֭הֹוָה וַחֲסָדֶ֑יךָ כִּ֖י מֵעוֹלָ֣ם הֵֽמָּה׃ יַֽעַנְךָ֣ יְ֭הֹוָה בְּי֣וֹם צָרָ֑ה יְ֝שַׂגֶּבְךָ֗ שֵׁ֤ם ׀ אֱלֹהֵ֬י יַעֲקֹֽב׃ יְהֹוָ֥ה הוֹשִׁ֑יעָה הַ֝מֶּ֗לֶךְ יַעֲנֵ֥נוּ בְיוֹם־קׇרְאֵֽנוּ: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ, חָנֵּנוּ וַעֲנֵנוּ כִּי אֵין בָּנוּ מַעֲשִׂים. עֲשֵׂה עִמָּנוּ צְדָקָה כְּרֹב רַחֲמֶיךָ, וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ:

parts.text: אֲדֹנָ֣י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֲשֶׁר֩ הוֹצֵ֨אתָ אֶֽת־עַמְּךָ֜ מֵאֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה וַתַּֽעַשׂ־לְךָ֥ שֵׁ֖ם כַּיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה חָטָ֖אנוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ׃ אֲדֹנָ֗י כְּכׇל־צִדְקֹתֶ֙ךָ֙ יָֽשׇׁב־נָ֤א אַפְּךָ֙ וַחֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ מֵעִֽירְךָ֥ יְרוּשָׁלַ֖‍ִם הַר־קׇדְשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּ֤י בַחֲטָאֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּבַעֲוֺנ֣וֹת אֲבֹתֵ֔ינוּ יְרוּשָׁלַ֧‍ִם וְעַמְּךָ֛ לְחֶרְפָּ֖ה לְכָל־סְבִיבֹתֵֽינוּ׃ וְעַתָּ֣ה ׀ שְׁמַ֣ע אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ אֶל־תְּפִלַּ֤ת עַבְדְּךָ֙ וְאֶל־תַּ֣חֲנוּנָ֔יו וְהָאֵ֣ר פָּנֶ֔יךָ עַל־מִקְדָּשְׁךָ֖ הַשָּׁמֵ֑ם לְמַ֖עַן אֲדֹנָֽי׃ הַטֵּ֨ה אֱלֹהַ֥י ׀ אׇזְנְךָ֮ וּֽשְׁמָע֒ פקחה [פְּקַ֣ח] עֵינֶ֗יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ שֹֽׁמְמֹתֵ֔ינוּ וְהָעִ֕יר אֲשֶׁר־נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עָלֶ֑יהָ כִּ֣י ׀ לֹ֣א עַל־צִדְקֹתֵ֗ינוּ אֲנַ֨חְנוּ מַפִּילִ֤ים תַּחֲנוּנֵ֙ינוּ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּ֖י עַל־רַחֲמֶ֥יךָ הָרַבִּֽים׃ אֲדֹנָ֤י ׀ שְׁמָ֙עָה֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י ׀ סְלָ֔חָה אֲדֹנָ֛י הַֽקְשִׁ֥יבָה וַעֲשֵׂ֖ה אַל־תְּאַחַ֑ר לְמַֽעַנְךָ֣ אֱלֹהַ֔י כִּֽי־שִׁמְךָ֣ נִקְרָ֔א עַל־עִירְךָ֖ וְעַל־עַמֶּֽךָ׃ אָבִינוּ אָב הָרַחֲמָן,

הַרְאֵנוּ אוֹת לְטוֹבָה וְקַבֵּץ נְפוּצוֹתֵינוּ מֵאַרְבַּע כַּנְפוֹת הָאָרֶץ. יַכִּירוּ וְיֵדְעוּ כָּל הַגּוֹיִם כִּי אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אָבִינוּ אָתָּה. אֲנַחְנוּ הַחֹמֶר וְאַתָּה יֹצְרֵנוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂה יָדְךָ כֻּלָּנוּ: אָבִינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ,

ח֧וּסָה יְהֹוָ֣ה עַל־עַמֶּ֗ךָ וְאַל־תִּתֵּ֨ן נַחֲלָתְךָ֤ לְחֶרְפָּה֙ לִמְשׇׁל־בָּ֣ם גּוֹיִ֔ם לָ֚מָּה יֹאמְר֣וּ בָעַמִּ֔ים אַיֵּ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃ יָדַעְנוּ יְהֹוָה כִּי חָטָאנוּ. וְאֵין מִי יַעֲמוֹד בַּעֲדֵנוּ אֶלָּא שִׁמְךָ הַגָּדוֹל יַעֲמוֹד לָנוּ בְּעֵת צָרָה. וּכְרַחֵם אָב עַל בָּנִים רַחֵם עָלֵינוּ. חֲמֹל עַל עַמָּךְ וְרַחֵם עַל נַחֲלָתָךְ. חוּסָה נָּא כְּרֹב רַחֲמֶיךָ חָנֵּנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ וַעֲנֵנוּ. לְךָ יְהֹוָה הַצְּדָקָה עוֹשֵׂה נִפְלָאוֹת בְּכָל עֵת וָעֵת. הַבֵּט נָא וְהוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא צֹאן מַרְעִיתֶךָ. אַל יִמְשָׁל בָּנוּ קֶצֶף כִּי לְךָ יְהֹוָה הַיְשׁוּעָה בְּךָ תוֹחַלְתֵּנוּ. אֱלוֹהַּ סְלִיחוֹת אָנָּא סְלַח נָא. כִּי אֵל טוֹב וְסַלָּח אָתָּה:

segs.text: אָנָּא מֶלֶךְ רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן, זְכוֹר וְהַבֵּט לִבְרִית בֵּין הַבְּתָרִים. וְתֵרָאֶה לְפָנֶיךָ עֲקֵדַת יָחִיד. וּלְמַעַן יִשְׂרָאֵל אָבִינוּ. אַל תַּעַזְבֵנוּ אָבִינוּ. וְאַל תִּטְּשֵׁנוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ וְאַל תִּשְׁכָּחֵנוּ יוֹצְרֵנוּ. וְאַל תַּעַשׂ עִמָּנוּ כָלָה בְּגָלוּתֵינוּ. כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אָתָּה:

אֵין כָּמוֹךָ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אֱלֹהֵינוּ. אֵין כָּמוֹךָ אֵל אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם וְרַב חֶסֶד וֶאֱמֶת. הושִׁיעֵנוּ וְרַחֲמֵנוּ מֵרַעַשׁ וּמֵרֹגֶז הַצִּילֵנוּ: זְכֹר֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֑ב אַל־תֵּ֗פֶן אֶל־קְשִׁי֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאֶל־רִשְׁע֖וֹ וְאֶל־חַטָּאתֽוֹ׃ שׁ֚וּב מֵחֲר֣וֹן אַפֶּ֔ךָ וְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל־הָרָעָ֖ה לְעַמֶּֽךָ׃ וְהָסֵר מִמֶּנּוּ מַכַּת הַמָּוֶת כִּי רַחוּם אָתָּה. כִּי כֵן דַּרְכְּךָ לַעֲשׂוֹת חֶסֶד חִנָּם בְּכָל דּוֹר וָדוֹר: אָנָּ֣א יְ֭הֹוָה הוֹשִׁ֘יעָ֥ה נָּ֑א אָנָּ֥א יְ֝הֹוָ֗ה הַצְלִ֘יחָ֥ה נָֽא׃ אָנָּא יְהֹוָה עֲנֵנוּ בְיוֹם קָרְאֵנוּ: לְךָ יְהֹוָה קִוִּינוּ. לְךָ יְהֹוָה חִכִּינוּ. לְךָ יְהֹוָה נְיַחֵל אַל תֶּחֱשֶׁה וּתְעַנֵּנוּ. כִּי נָאֲמוּ גוֹיִם אָבְדָה תִקְוָתָם. כָּל בֶּרֶךְ לְךָ תִכְרַע וְכָל קוֹמָה לְפָנֶיךָ תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה:

הַפּוֹתֵחַ יָד בִּתְשׁוּבָה לְקַבֵּל פּוֹשְׁעִים וְחַטָּאִים. נִבְהֲלָה נַפְשֵׁנוּ מֵרוֹב עִצְּבוֹנֵנוּ. אַל תִּשְׁכָּחֵנוּ נֶצַח קוּמָה וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ. אַל תִּשְׁפּוֹךְ חֲרוֹנְךָ עָלֵינוּ כִּי עַמְּךָ אֲנַחְנוּ בְּנֵי בְרִיתֶךָ. אֵל הַבִּיטָה. דַּל כְּבוֹדֵנוּ בַגּוֹיִם וְשִׁקְּצוּנוּ כְּטֻמְאַת הַנִּדָּה. עַד מָתַי עֻזְּךָ בַּשְּׁבִי וְתִפְאַרְתְּךָ בְּיַד צָר. הֵמָּה יִרְאוּ וְיֵבשׁוּ וְיֵחַתּוּ מִגְּבוּרָתָם. עוֹרְרָה גְבוּרָתְךָ וְהוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ לְמַעַן שְׁמֶךָ. אַל יִמְעֲטוּ לְפָנֶיךָ תְּלָאוֹתֵינוּ מַהֵר יְקַדְּמוּנוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ בְּעֵת צָרוֹתֵנוּ. לֹא לְמַעֲנֵנוּ אֶלָּא לְמַעֲנָךְ פְּעֹל וְאַל תַּשְׁחֵת אֶת זֵכֶר שְׁאֵרִיתֵנוּ. כִּי לְךָ מְיַחֲלוֹת עֵינֵינוּ כִּי אֵל מֶלֶךְ חַנּוּן וְרַחוּם אָתָּה. וּזְכוֹר עֵדוּתֵינוּ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד אוֹמְרִים פַּעֲמַיִם בְּאַהֲבָה: שְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יְהֹוָ֥ה ׀ אֶחָֽד׃

segs.en: And the chazzan says Half Kaddish, the Torah is taken out and three people are called up, and the prayer is concluded as on any other day. After Hoshi'enu, they say Shir Mizmor LaAsaf, Elohim El Dami Lecha.
segs.text: <small>ואומר הש"ץ חצי קדיש, ומוציאים ס"ת וקוראים ג' עולים, וגומרים התפלה כבכל יום, ואחר הושיענו אומרים שיר מזמור לאסף, אלהים אל דמי לך.</small>

And to the ground my eminence has been brought low, on the day the wicked one thought to subdue me. The joy of my heart has ceased, and I was cast out from my resting place; my gates sigh and mourn, on the day my nobles and my dignitaries were taken away. Therefore I lament year after year in the fourth month.

In the fourth month evils and sighs encompassed me, on the seventeenth of it. I am weary with my sighing and have found no rest; I cried out and cried out in weeping, and every head is bald with mourning, for on this day the Tablets were broken. The Tablets left me, and troubles surrounded me; the hand of my adversary grew strong and scattered me to every corner. Turn, please, and shield those who wait for the end of wonders, for Hashem of Hosts is a sun and a shield.

In the fourth month I thought I would come up from the miry deep, where there is no foothold; on the seventeenth of it I became a thing of scorn, to be devoured and destroyed, and I found no rest, my pains ever before me, for on it the daily offering was abolished. The day the daily offering was taken away, my wailing grew like the wailing of Eglaim, and my mourning grew as great as the mourning at Hadad-rimmon, doubled. Turn, please, and revive our slumbering ones, God who dwells in heaven; after two days may He revive us.

In the fourth month I bore the wrath of the Rock, and His fury burned in me; on the seventeenth of it trembling seized me and a storm raged. I forgot good things, and my soul was cast far from peace in the strife of Seir, for on it the city was breached. The day the city was breached, when Teiman and Magdiel arose, my hand grew slack and found no power in God. Turn, please, and sanctify the remnant of Ariel; let them sanctify the Holy One of Jacob and stand in awe of the God of Israel.

In the fourth month, a day of woe, a day of rebuke and wrath; on the seventeenth of it my glory went into exile and my splendor was removed. There is no healing for my break, my wound is grievous and my spirit is broken, for on it Apostomos burned the Torah. The day the Torah was burned, my sorrows were renewed, and my elders and my aged ones ceased from the holy city. Turn, please, and be gracious in Your might to the congregation of my faithful ones, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of Hashem.

In the fourth month a stranger measured out my crookedness, in measure upon measure; on the seventeenth of it the stranger laid waste the pleasantness of the Name and devoured Jacob. Year after year on this day I eat bitter herbs, for on it an idol was set up in the Sanctuary. The day the idol of jealousy and abomination was set up, my spirit was ruined on it and my hope disappointed. Turn, please, and heal the backsliding of Your people, and love them freely; bring us back, Hashem, to You, and we shall return.

Through Your abundant mercies, forgive us, our Father, for in the multitude of our folly we have erred; pardon us, our King, for our iniquities are many. You are a God slow to anger, and You have taught us the way of repentance. Remember today the greatness of Your mercies and Your kindnesses for the descendants of Your beloved. Turn to us with compassion, for You are the Master of compassion. With supplication and prayer we come before You, as You made known to the humble one of old. Turn back from Your burning anger, as it is written in Your Torah. In the shadow of Your wings we take refuge and find shelter, as on the day when “Hashem descended in a cloud”; pass over transgression and pardon guilt, as on the day when “He stood with him there”; hear our cry and give ear favorably to our plea, as on the day when “he proclaimed the name of Hashem.” And there it is said:

“Hashem passed before him and proclaimed: Hashem, Hashem, God, merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands of generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and absolving.”

Then, when I was faithless, says the One who dwells in my dwelling, when my iniquity was entwined and my reckoner made my yoke heavy, a stranger overcame me to beat me with his blows; his anger tore at me, and he hated me. I abandoned His ways, which He had taught me; therefore He roused against me anger, rage and wrath. He emptied out His fury upon me and shot His arrows at me, and set me up as His target. On this day five hardships passed over me; they tore apart my life and made me a ruin. My soul is weary to the point of expiring, and exhausted; I am bent from hearing and confounded by seeing. When I remember all these, sighs rouse me; a flame has scorched me, kindling my loins and inner parts; I raise a bitter lament and keep joys far away, for on this day the Tablets were broken. A stranger assembled against me and joined his multitudes; they surrounded me like water and I sank, with none to uphold me. Therefore I wail with my own mouth and lament continually, for on this day the daily offering was abolished. My oppressors roared like the roar of a stream; they cut off my life in the pit and gave me as food. He summoned a time against me, and my multitudes were bereaved, utterly bereaved, for on this day an idol was set up in the Sanctuary. I who was great with people, a stranger besieged her and laid bare her gates; he made my vine a desolation on the day of fury and wrath. The stranger saw his desire fulfilled, and his hand grew strong with might, for on this day Apostomos burned the Torah.

Wicked ones gnashed their teeth on the day Hashem’s anger roused against me; the stranger and the crooked one had no pity on old or young. His anger burned against me and He kindled His flames in me, for on this day the city was breached. Have mercy, Hashem, and speak to the heart of those who grieve, who sit desolate on the seventeenth of the month. Yah, roll upon them the multitude of Your mercies from on high, God, King who sits on the throne of mercy.

Look upon the one bound, who was delivered into the hand of Babylon and the governor of the city; he moans to You, how long, and entreats like the youngest son. Before You, Rock, with a pent-up heart, he stirs the moaning of his inner being: the day the enemy grew strong and the city was breached. For this I bend and clap my hands, for on the fifth day they called me; and because of the calf, the Tablets left me. The stranger captured the fortress and brought me into confinement; he also abolished the daily offering, and kept me from performing it. An idol was set up in the Sanctuary entire, and the stranger burned Your law in fire. I am seized with great pain and trembling, on the day Shaddai stripped me bare. And the serpent from the north swept me away like a flood; he led the captives of the land of splendor and wound me up like a ball. A day of darkness, when the light was darkened; he pushed me into the hand of Persia. He consumed me and appalled me, and over this I will raise a dirge. Will it be forever, my Refuge? Will Your anger smoke forever? Repair my breach through the son of Perez, and from the thorn gather the lily. Open Your eye, take my prayer like the fat of the fattened. Build the Sanctuary, and return the border, the Carmel and the Bashan. Judge the mute, and then He will repay the one who caused the burning and the one who kindled the fire.

God of our salvation, heed our cry, and see our desolation and the length of our exile, year after year, as we remember our affliction on the day on which five things befell our fathers. Please, God of spirits and Examiner of hidden depths, look upon the scattered flock, cast out to the four winds, sighing at this season year after year; on the day of the thrust, the Tablets were broken, and on it all the days of our years we embitter ourselves over our sorrow. Draw us out of the mire of the deep, where we have sunk with none to stand us up; You gave the flock as food, as scorn and destruction. Year after year on this day sorrow clings to us; the day on which a stranger’s hand was raised, and on it the daily offering was abolished, because of our many iniquities and the greatness of our sins. Yah, who can do all things, redeem us from bereavement and loss, from the hand of the crooked and the foolish who devoured the remnant of Jacob. Year after year on this day I eat bitter herbs, when a stranger set up before me an idol in the Sanctuary; over all that has befallen us our tears flow. How awesome is our breaking, for we turned aside from fear of You; the Radiant One, robed in light, has taught the recompense to all. Year after year I lament on this day, because on it Apostomos burned the Torah; for this we lie down in our shame, over the plunder of the house of our glory. The Compassionate One forgives iniquity and does not arouse all His wrath; swiftly redeem from the hand of Seir the scattered ones of the flock and the young. Year after year on this day His inner being stirs, the day the strangers prevailed and the city was breached, for we were a mockery and a derision to those around us. Merciful One, return in mercy to afflicted Zion, and hasten, please, to the sorrowing woman the promised consolation; and then we shall bring forth song when You rebuild the ruin, in the gathering of our dispersed, and when You return our captivity.

God, King who sits on the throne of mercy, who acts with loving-kindness, who pardons the iniquities of His people, who removes sins one by one, who increases forgiveness for sinners and pardon for transgressors, who deals righteously with all flesh and spirit, who does not repay them according to their deeds. God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen [Attributes], and remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen, as You made known to the humble one of old, as it is written: “Hashem descended in a cloud and stood with him there, and He proclaimed the name of Hashem.” And there it is said:

“Hashem passed before him and proclaimed: Hashem, Hashem, God, merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands of generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and absolving.”

Men of faith have perished, those who came by the strength of their deeds, mighty to stand in the breach, who turned away the decrees. They were a wall for us, and a refuge on the day of wrath. They extinguished anger with their whispered prayer and held back fury with their cry. Before they called You, You answered them; they knew how to entreat and to appease. As a father You had compassion for their sake; You did not turn their faces away empty. Through our many iniquities we lost them; they were gathered away from us through our sins. They have gone to their rest and left us to sighing. The builders of the fence have ceased; those who turned back wrath are cut off. None is left standing in the breach; those worthy of appeasing You have ceased. We have wandered to the four corners; we found no remedy. We have come back to You in shame, to seek You, God, in the time of our troubles.

God, King who sits on the throne of mercy, who acts with loving-kindness, who pardons the iniquities of His people, who removes sins one by one, who increases forgiveness for sinners and pardon for transgressors, who deals righteously with all flesh and spirit, who does not repay them according to their deeds. God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen [Attributes], and remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen, as You made known to the humble one of old, as it is written: “Hashem descended in a cloud and stood with him there, and He proclaimed the name of Hashem.” And there it is said:

“Hashem passed before him and proclaimed: Hashem, Hashem, God, merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands of generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and absolving.”

We are astounded by evils; our strength has failed from troubles. We have sunk exceedingly low; we have been brought down to the dust. Merciful One, such is our nature: we are stiff-necked and rebellious. We cried out with our mouths, “We have sinned,” and our heart is crooked and twisted. Most High, Your mercies are from of old; forgiveness is with You. Relent from the evil; incline toward kindness. Do not hide Yourself in times of trouble, O God, for we are in great distress. Let Your goodness and Your kindness toward us be known before the eyes of all. Seal the mouth of the accuser, and let him not accuse us; rage against him, and let him be silenced. Let a good advocate arise to vindicate us; let him declare our uprightness. Your ways, Merciful and Gracious One, You revealed to the faithful one of the house; when he sought them from You then, You made Your faithfulness known to him.

God, King who sits on the throne of mercy, who acts with loving-kindness, who pardons the iniquities of His people, who removes sins one by one, who increases forgiveness for sinners and pardon for transgressors, who deals righteously with all flesh and spirit, who does not repay them according to their deeds. God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen [Attributes], and remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen, as You made known to the humble one of old, as it is written: “Hashem descended in a cloud and stood with him there, and He proclaimed the name of Hashem.” And there it is said:

“Hashem passed before him and proclaimed: Hashem, Hashem, God, merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands of generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and absolving.”

When Israel sinned in the wilderness, Moses stood in prayer before You and sought mercy for Your people Israel, and this is what he said in his prayer: “Pardon, please, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of Your kindness, and as You have borne this people from Egypt until now.” And You, too, answered him in Your good ways, bringing him good tidings and showing him grace, and You said to him: “I have pardoned, as you have asked.”

Daniel, the man most beloved, said before You: “Incline Your ear, my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see our desolation, and the city upon which Your name is called; for not on account of our righteousness do we lay our supplications before You, but on account of Your abundant mercies. My Lord, hear; my Lord, forgive; my Lord, attend and act; do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, for Your name is called upon Your city and upon Your people.” You said to her: “Behold, I will enter into judgment with you for your saying, ‘I have not sinned.’” We are ashamed of our deeds and humiliated by our iniquities; we have no mouth to answer and no boldness to lift our heads.

Our God and God of our fathers, do not make an end of us. Withhold Your hand in judgment when reproof comes before You; do not blot out our name from Your book. Come close to investigate [our] discipline; may Your mercies precede Your anger. Observe our poor deeds; bring righteousness near of Your own accord. Instruct us when we cry to You; command our salvation through the Intercessor. Restore the captivity of the tents of the perfect; see their gates, for they are desolate. Remember the faithful testimony; do not forget it from the mouth of his seed. Loosen the sealed testimony; place Your secret in our learning, the center of the rounded basin: let the mixed wine not be lacking. Yah, know Israel, who have known You; cast down the nations that have not known You. For You will restore to the stronghold the prisoners of hope.

We are guiltier than any people, more ashamed than any nation. Joy has departed from us; our heart is sick through our sins. Our desire has been ruined and our glory stripped away; the dwelling of our Sanctuary lies in ruins through our iniquities. Our palace has become desolate; the beauty of our land is given to strangers, our strength to foreigners. Before our eyes our toil was plundered; what we had was drawn and stripped from us. A yoke was set upon us and we bore it on our shoulder; slaves ruled over us, and none could free us from their hand. Many troubles surrounded us; we called to You, Hashem our God. You were far from us because of our iniquities; we turned back from following You, we strayed like sheep and were lost. And we have not yet turned from our error. How then can we brazenly stiffen our necks, to say before You, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, “We are righteous and have not sinned”?

Ezra the scribe said before You: “My God, I am ashamed and humiliated to lift my face to You, my God, for our iniquities have risen above our heads, and our guilt has grown up to the heavens.” But You are a God of pardons, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in kindness, and You did not forsake them. Do not forsake us, our Father; do not abandon us, our King; do not forget us, our Maker; and do not make an end of us in our exile. And fulfill for us, Hashem our God, the word You promised us through Jeremiah, Your seer, as it is said: “In those days and at that time, declares Hashem, the iniquity of Israel will be sought, and there will be none, and the sins of Judah, and they will not be found, for I will pardon those whom I leave.” Let no sin or iniquity stand in the way of our prayer before You, and pardon and forgive all our iniquities, for You are a good and forgiving God.

What shall we say before You, You who dwell on high, and what shall we recount before You, You who abide in the heavens? Is it not that You know all that is hidden and all that is revealed? You know the secrets of the world and the hidden mysteries of every living being. You search all the chambers of the belly; You see the kidneys and the heart. Nothing is hidden from You, and nothing is concealed from before Your eyes.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that You forgive us all our sins, atone for all our iniquities, and pardon and forgive all our transgressions; and pardon our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving, abounding in kindness to all who call upon You. For Your name’s sake, Hashem, pardon my iniquity, for it is great. For Your name’s sake, Hashem, You will give me life; in Your righteousness bring my soul out of trouble. Hashem of Hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah. Hashem of Hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You. Hashem, save! May the King answer us on the day we call. Bring us back to You, Hashem, and we shall return; renew our days as of old.

And He, the Merciful, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; He often turns back His anger and does not stir up all His wrath. You, Hashem, will not withhold Your mercies from me; Your kindness and Your truth will always guard me. Save us, Hashem our God, and gather us from the nations, to give thanks to Your holy Name and to glory in Your praise. If You, Yah, should keep iniquities, Lord, who could stand? For with You is forgiveness, so that You may be feared. He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our iniquities. If our iniquities testify against us, Hashem, act for Your name’s sake. Remember Your mercies, Hashem, and Your kindnesses, for they are from of old. May Hashem answer you on the day of trouble; may the name of the God of Jacob protect you. Hashem, save! May the King answer us on the day we call. Our Father, our King, be gracious to us and answer us, for we have no worthy deeds; deal with us in charity according to Your abundant mercy, and save us for Your name’s sake.

And now, my Lord our God, who brought Your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for Yourself, as this very day—we have sinned, we have acted wickedly. My Lord, according to all Your righteous acts, let Your anger and Your wrath turn away from Your city Jerusalem, Your holy mountain; for because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people have become a reproach to all around us. And now, our God, hear the prayer of Your servant and his supplications, and cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate Sanctuary, for the sake of the Lord. Incline Your ear, my God, and hear; open Your eyes and see our desolation, and the city upon which Your name is called; for not on account of our righteousness do we lay our supplications before You, but on account of Your abundant mercy. My Lord, hear; my Lord, forgive; my Lord, listen and act, do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, for Your name is called upon Your city and Your people. Our Father, merciful Father, show us a sign for good, and gather our scattered ones from the four corners of the earth. Let all the nations recognize and know that You, Hashem, are our Father. We are the clay and You are our Potter, and we are all the work of Your hand. Our Father, our King, our Rock and our Redeemer, spare Your people, Hashem, and do not make Your inheritance a reproach, for the nations to rule over them. Why should they say among the peoples, “Where is their God?” We know, Hashem, that we have sinned, and there is no one to stand up for us but Your great Name; let it stand by us in time of trouble. As a father has compassion for his children, have compassion on us. Pity Your people and have mercy on Your inheritance. Spare us, please, in Your abundant mercy; be gracious to us, our King, and answer us. Yours, Hashem, is righteousness; You work wonders at all times. Look, please, and save, please, the flock of Your pasture. Let no wrath rule over us, for Yours, Hashem, is the salvation; in You is our hope. God of forgiveness, please, forgive. For You are a good and forgiving God.

We beseech You, gracious and compassionate King: remember and look to the Covenant between the Pieces, and let the binding of the only one appear before You, and for the sake of Israel our father. Do not abandon us, our Father; do not cast us off, our King; do not forget us, our Maker; and do not make an end of us in our exile. For You are a gracious and compassionate God and King.

There is none like You, gracious and compassionate, our God; there is none like You, God slow to anger and abounding in kindness and truth. Save us and have mercy on us; from tumult and wrath deliver us. Remember Your servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; do not look to the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, nor to their sin. Turn from Your burning anger and relent from the evil to Your people. And remove from us the plague of death, for You are compassionate; for such is Your way, to do kindness freely in every generation. Please, Hashem, save us, please; please, Hashem, grant us success, please. Please, Hashem, answer us on the day we call. For You, Hashem, we have hoped; for You, Hashem, we have waited; for You, Hashem, we have longed; do not be silent, and answer us. For the nations say: their hope is lost. Every knee shall bow to You, and every upright one shall prostrate before You.

You who open Your hand in repentance to receive transgressors and sinners: our soul is dismayed by the abundance of our sorrow. Do not forget us forever; arise and save us. Do not pour out Your wrath upon us, for we are Your people, the children of Your covenant. God, look! Our honor has been diminished among the nations, and they abhor us as something impure. How long will Your strength be in captivity, and Your glory in the hand of the foe? Let them see and be ashamed, let them be dismayed at their might. Awaken Your might and save us for the sake of Your Name. Let our troubles not be small before You; let Your mercies quickly come to meet us in the time of our distress. Not for our sake but for Yours, act, and do not destroy the remembrance of our remnant. For our eyes look to You, for You are a gracious and compassionate God and King. And remember our testimony every day continually, we who say twice daily with love: “Hear, O Israel, Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.”

segs.en: Mourning
segs.text: אבלות

segs.en: For the seven close relatives, one must tear while standing, and before tearing, recite the blessing:
segs.text: <small>על ז' קרובים צריך לקרוע מעומד, ולפני שיקרע יברך:</small>
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, דַּיָּן הָאֱמֶת:

segs.en: Justification of the Judgment
segs.text: צידוק הדין

parts.text: צַדִּ֣יק אַתָּ֣ה יְהֹוָ֑ה וְ֝יָשָׁ֗ר מִשְׁפָּטֶֽיךָ׃ צַדִּ֣יק יְ֭הֹוָה בְּכׇל־דְּרָכָ֑יו וְ֝חָסִ֗יד בְּכׇל־מַעֲשָֽׂיו׃ צִדְקָתְךָ֣ צֶ֣דֶק לְעוֹלָ֑ם וְֽתוֹרָתְךָ֥ אֱמֶֽת׃ מִֽשְׁפְּטֵי־יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱמֶ֑ת צָֽדְק֥וּ יַחְדָּֽו׃ בַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר דְּבַר־מֶ֖לֶךְ שִׁלְט֑וֹן וּמִ֥י יֹֽאמַר־ל֖וֹ מַֽה־תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃ וְה֣וּא בְ֭אֶחָד וּמִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נּוּ וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹ אִוְּתָ֣ה וַיָּֽעַשׂ׃ קָטֹ֣ן וְ֭גָדוֹל שָׁ֣ם ה֑וּא וְ֝עֶ֗בֶד חׇפְשִׁ֥י מֵאֲדֹנָֽיו׃ הֵ֣ן בַּ֭עֲבָדָיו לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ין וּ֝בְמַלְאָכָ֗יו יָשִׂ֥ים תׇּהֳלָֽה׃ אַ֤ף ׀ שֹׁכְנֵ֬י בָֽתֵּי־חֹ֗מֶר אֲשֶׁר־בֶּעָפָ֥ר יְסוֹדָ֑ם יְ֝דַכְּא֗וּם לִפְנֵי־עָֽשׁ׃ הַצּוּר֙ תָּמִ֣ים פׇּֽעֳל֔וֹ כִּ֥י כׇל־דְּרָכָ֖יו מִשְׁפָּ֑ט אֵ֤ל אֱמוּנָה֙ וְאֵ֣ין עָ֔וֶל צַדִּ֥יק וְיָשָׁ֖ר הֽוּא׃ דַּיַּן הָאֱמֶת,

כִּי כָל־מִשְׁפָּטָיו צֶדֶק וֶאֱמֶת:

הַמְרַחֵם עַל־כָּל־בְּרִיּוֹתָיו הוּא יָחוּס וְיַחְמוֹל וִירַחֵם עַל נֶפֶשׁ רוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה שֶׁל (פב"פ) רוּחַ ה' תְּנִיחֶנּוּ (

בִּלַּ֤ע הַמָּ֨וֶת֙ לָנֶ֔צַח וּמָחָ֨ה אֲדֹנָ֧י יֱהֹוִ֛ה דִּמְעָ֖ה מֵעַ֣ל כׇּל־פָּנִ֑ים וְחֶרְפַּ֣ת עַמּ֗וֹ יָסִיר֙ מֵעַ֣ל כׇּל־הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ יִֽחְי֣וּ מֵתֶ֔יךָ נְבֵלָתִ֖י יְקוּמ֑וּן הָקִ֨יצוּ וְרַנְּנ֜וּ שֹׁכְנֵ֣י עָפָ֗ר כִּ֣י טַ֤ל אוֹרֹת֙ טַלֶּ֔ךָ וָאָ֖רֶץ רְפָאִ֥ים תַּפִּֽיל׃ וְה֤וּא רַח֨וּם ׀ יְכַפֵּ֥ר עָוֺן֮ וְֽלֹא־יַֽ֫שְׁחִ֥ית וְ֭הִרְבָּה לְהָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ וְלֹא־יָ֝עִ֗יר כׇּל־חֲמָתֽוֹ׃ יְהֹוָ֥ה הוֹשִׁ֑יעָה הַ֝מֶּ֗לֶךְ יַעֲנֵ֥נוּ בְיוֹם־קׇרְאֵֽנוּ:

parts.en: Until the end of the seven days.

segs.text: <small>ואחר כך אומרים</small>

parts.text: מִזְמ֗וֹר לְדָ֫וִ֥ד יְ֭הֹוָה מִי־יָג֣וּר בְּאׇהֳלֶ֑ךָ מִֽי־יִ֝שְׁכֹּ֗ן בְּהַ֣ר קׇדְשֶֽׁךָ׃ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ תָּ֭מִים וּפֹעֵ֥ל צֶ֑דֶק וְדֹבֵ֥ר אֱ֝מֶ֗ת בִּלְבָבֽוֹ׃ לֹֽא־רָגַ֨ל ׀ עַל־לְשֹׁנ֗וֹ לֹא־עָשָׂ֣ה לְרֵעֵ֣הוּ רָעָ֑ה וְ֝חֶרְפָּ֗ה לֹא־נָשָׂ֥א עַל־קְרֹבֽוֹ׃ נִבְזֶ֤ה ׀ בְּֽעֵ֘ינָ֤יו נִמְאָ֗ס וְאֶת־יִרְאֵ֣י יְהֹוָ֣ה יְכַבֵּ֑ד נִשְׁבַּ֥ע לְ֝הָרַ֗ע וְלֹ֣א יָמִֽר׃ כַּסְפּ֤וֹ ׀ לֹא־נָתַ֣ן בְּנֶשֶׁךְ֮ וְשֹׁ֥חַד עַל־נָקִ֗י לֹ֥א לָ֫קָ֥חעֹֽשֵׂה־אֵ֑לֶּה לֹ֖א יִמּ֣וֹט לְעוֹלָֽם׃

מִכְתָּ֥ם לְדָוִ֑ד שׇֽׁמְרֵ֥נִי אֵ֝֗ל כִּֽי־חָסִ֥יתִי בָֽךְ׃ אָמַ֣רְתְּ לַֽ֭יהֹוָה אֲדֹנָ֣י אָ֑תָּה ט֝וֹבָתִ֗י בַּל־עָלֶֽיךָ׃ לִ֭קְדוֹשִׁים אֲשֶׁר־בָּאָ֣רֶץ הֵ֑מָּה וְ֝אַדִּירֵ֗י כׇּל־חֶפְצִי־בָֽם׃ יִרְבּ֥וּ עַצְּבוֹתָם֮ אַחֵ֢ר מָ֫הָ֥רוּ בַּל־אַסִּ֣יךְ נִסְכֵּיהֶ֣ם מִדָּ֑ם וּֽבַל־אֶשָּׂ֥א אֶת־שְׁ֝מוֹתָ֗ם עַל־שְׂפָתָֽי׃ יְֽהֹוָ֗ה מְנָת־חֶלְקִ֥י וְכוֹסִ֑י אַ֝תָּ֗ה תּוֹמִ֥יךְ גּוֹרָלִֽי׃ חֲבָלִ֣ים נָֽפְלוּ־לִ֭י בַּנְּעִמִ֑ים אַף־נַ֝חֲלָ֗ת שָֽׁפְרָ֥ה עָלָֽי׃ אֲבָרֵ֗ךְ אֶת־יְ֭הֹוָה אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְעָצָ֑נִי אַף־לֵ֝יל֗וֹת יִסְּר֥וּנִי כִלְיוֹתָֽי׃ שִׁוִּ֬יתִי יְהֹוָ֣ה לְנֶגְדִּ֣י תָמִ֑יד כִּ֥י מִֽ֝ימִינִ֗י בַּל־אֶמּֽוֹט׃ לָכֵ֤ן ׀ שָׂמַ֣ח לִ֭בִּי וַיָּ֣גֶל כְּבוֹדִ֑י אַף־בְּ֝שָׂרִ֗י יִשְׁכֹּ֥ן לָבֶֽטַח׃ כִּ֤י ׀ לֹא־תַעֲזֹ֣ב נַפְשִׁ֣י לִשְׁא֑וֹל לֹֽא־תִתֵּ֥ן חֲ֝סִידְךָ֗ לִרְא֥וֹת שָֽׁחַת׃ תּֽוֹדִיעֵנִי֮ אֹ֤רַח חַ֫יִּ֥ים שֹׂ֣בַע שְׂ֭מָחוֹת אֶת־פָּנֶ֑יךָ נְעִמ֖וֹת בִּימִינְךָ֣ נֶֽצַח׃

If there are three, they say:

parts.text: (אֱלֹהֵינוּ)</small> מְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים שֶׁאָכַלְנוּ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ וּבְטוּבוֹ הַגָּדוֹל חָיִֽינוּ:
(אֱלֹהֵינוּ)</small> מְנַחֵם אֲבֵלִים שֶׁאָכַלְנוּ מִשֶּׁלּוֹ וּבְטוּבוֹ הַגָּדוֹל חָיִֽינוּ:

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה. אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם. הָאֵל הַזָּן אוֹתָֽנוּ וְאֶת־הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ בְּטוּבוֹ. בְּחֵן בְּחֶֽסֶד בְּרֶֽוַח וּבְרַחֲמִים רַבִּים. נֹתֵ֣ן לֶ֭חֶם לְכָל־בָּשָׂ֑ר כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ. וּבְטוּבוֹ הַגָּדוֹל תָּמִיד לֹא חָֽסַר לָֽנוּ. וְאַל־יֶחְסַר לָֽנוּ מָזוֹן תָּמִיד לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. כִּי הוּא אֵל זָן וּמְפַרְנֵס לַכֹּל. וְשֻׁלְחָנוֹ עָרוּךְ לַכֹּל. וְהִתְקִין מִחְיָה וּמָזוֹן לְכָל־בְּרִיּוֹתָיו אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא בְּרַחֲמָיו וּבְרוֹב חֲסָדָיו. כָּאָמוּר. פּוֹתֵ֥חַ אֶת־יָדֶ֑ךָ

parts.en: (Acrostic of the letters of the name of God and the number of the letters of the Torah)
parts.text: <small>(ר"ת פא"י שהוא מספר יאהדונהי ומספר סא"ל וס"ת חת"ך)</small>

parts.en: (As the number of the letters of the Torah)

parts.text: לְכָל־חַ֣י רָצֽוֹן. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה. הַזָּן אֶת־הַכֹּל:

segs.text: נוֹדֶה לְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ עַל שֶׁהִנְחַֽלְתָּ לַאֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ. אֶֽרֶץ חֶמְדָּה טוֹבָה וּרְחָבָה. בְּרִית וְתוֹרָה חַיִּים וּמָזוֹן. עַל שֶׁהוֹצֵאתָֽנוּ מֵאֶֽרֶץ מִצְרַֽיִם. וּפְדִיתָֽנוּ מִבֵּית עֲבָדִים. וְעַל בְּרִֽיתְךָֽ שֶׁחָתַֽמְתָּ בִּבְשָׂרֵֽנוּ. וְעַל תּוֹרָֽתְךָֽ שֶׁלִּמַּדְתָּֽנוּ. וְעַל חֻקֵּי רְצוֹנָךְ שֶׁהוֹדַעְתָּֽנוּ. וְעַל חַיִּים וּמָזוֹן שֶׁאַתָּה זָן וּמְפַרְנֵס אוֹתָֽנוּ:

segs.en: On Chanukah and Purim, add here about the miracles.
segs.text: <small>בחנוכה ופורים מוסיפים כאן על הנסים</small>

עַל הַכֹּל יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ אֲנַֽחְנוּ מוֹדִים לָךְ. וּמְבָֽרְכִֽים אֶת־שְׁמָךְ. כָּאָמוּר. וְאָֽכַלְתָּ֖ וְשָׂבָ֑עְתָּ וּבֵֽרַכְתָּ֙ אֶת־יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ עַל־הָאָ֥רֶץ הַטֹּבָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָֽתַן־לָֽךְ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה. עַל הָאָֽרֶץ וְעַל הַמָּזוֹן:

parts.text: רַחֵם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ עָלֵֽינוּ וְעַל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַמָּךְ. וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלַֽיִם עִירָךְ. וְעַל הַר צִיּוֹן מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדָךְ. וְעַל הֵיכָלָךְ. וְעַל מְעוֹנָךְ. וְעַל דְּבִירָךְ. וְעַל הַבַּֽיִת הַגָּדוֹל וְהַקָּדוֹשׁ שֶׁנִּקְרָא שִׁמְךָ עָלָיו. אָבִֽינוּ. רְעֵֽנוּ. זוּנֵֽנוּ. פַּרְנְסֵֽנוּ. כַּלְכְּלֵֽנוּ. הַרְוִיחֵֽנוּ הַרְוַח־לָֽנוּ מְהֵרָה מִכָּל־צָרוֹתֵֽינוּ. וְנָא. אַל תַּצְרִיכֵֽנוּ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ. לִידֵי מַתְּנוֹת בָּשָׂר וָדָם וְלֹא לִידֵי הַלְוָאָתָם. אֶלָּא לְיָֽדְךָֽ הַמְּלֵאָה וְהָרְחָבָה. הָעֲשִׁירָה וְהַפְּתוּחָה. יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נֵבוֹשׁ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה. וְלֹא נִכָּלֵם לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא. וּמַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד מְשִׁיחָךְ תַּחֲזִירֶֽנָּה לִמְקוֹמָהּ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵֽינוּ:

parts.en: On Shabbat, say Retzei here; on Rosh Chodesh, say Ya'aleh VeYavo.
parts.text: <small>בשבת אומרים כאן רצה, ובראש חדש יעלה ויבא</small>

segs.text:
נַחֵם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ אֶת־אֲבֵלֵי צִיּוֹן וְאֶת־אֲבֵלֵי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם וְאֶת־הָאֲבֵלִים הַמִּתְאַבְּלִים בָּאֵבֶל הַזֶּה נַחֲמֵם מֵאֶבְלָם וְשַׂמְּחֵם מִיגוֹנָם. כָּאָמוּר: כְּאִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִמּ֖וֹ תְּנַחֲמֶ֑נּוּ כֵּ֤ן אָֽנֹכִי֙ אֲנַ֣חֶמְכֶ֔ם וּבִירֽוּשָׁלַ֖‍ִם תְּנֻחָֽמוּ׃ בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה מְנַחֵם צִיּוֹן בְּבִנְיַן יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אָמֵן:
בְּחַיֵּֽינוּ תִּבְנֶה עִיר צִיּוֹן וְתִכּוֹן הָעֲבוֹדָה בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם:

parts.text: הָאֵל אָבִֽינוּ מַלְכֵּנוּ אַדִּירֵנוּ גֹּאֲלֵנוּ קְדוֹשֵׁנוּ קְדוֹשׁ יַעֲקֹב. הַמֶּלֶךְ הַחַי הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב אֵל אֱמֶת שׁוֹפֵט בְּצֶדֶק לוֹקֵחַ נְפָשׁוֹת שַׁלִּיט בְּעוֹלָמוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כִּרְצוֹנוֹ וַאֲנַחְנוּ עַמּוֹ וַעֲבָדָיו וְעַל הַכֹּל אֲנַחְנוּ חַיָּיבִים לְהוֹדוֹת לוֹ וּלְבָֽרְכוֹ גּוֹדֵר פְּרָצוֹת הוּא יִגְדּוֹר אֶת־הַפִּרְצָה הַזֹּאת מֵעָלֵֽינוּ וּמֵעַל עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּרַחֲמִים.

segs.en: Laying to Rest for a Man
segs.text: השכבה לאיש

parts.text: הוּא יָחוּס וְיַחְמוֹל וִירַחֵם עַל נֶפֶשׁ רוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה שֶׁל

segs.en: For a great man of Torah and fear of Heaven, they say:
segs.text: <small>לאדם גדול בתורה וביראת שמים אומרים</small>

וְֽ֭הַחׇכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תִּמָּצֵ֑א וְאֵ֥י זֶ֗֝ה מְק֣וֹם בִּינָֽה׃ אַשְׁרֵ֣י אָ֭דָם מָצָ֣א חׇכְמָ֑ה וְ֝אָדָ֗ם יָפִ֥יק תְּבוּנָֽה׃ מָ֤ה רַֽב־טוּבְךָ֮ אֲשֶׁר־צָפַ֢נְתָּ לִּירֵ֫אֶ֥יךָ פָּ֭עַלְתָּ לַחֹסִ֣ים בָּ֑ךְ נֶ֗֝גֶד בְּנֵ֣י אָדָֽם׃ מַה־יָּקָ֥ר חַסְדְּךָ֗ אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים וּבְנֵ֥י אָדָ֑ם בְּצֵ֥ל כְּ֝נָפֶ֗יךָ יֶחֱסָיֽוּן׃ יִ֭רְוְיֻן מִדֶּ֣שֶׁן בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ וְנַ֖חַל עֲדָנֶ֣יךָ תַשְׁקֵֽם׃ ט֥וֹב שֵׁ֖ם מִשֶּׁ֣מֶן ט֑וֹב וְי֣וֹם הַמָּ֔וֶת מִיּ֖וֹם הִוָּלְדֽוֹ׃ ס֥וֹף דָּבָ֖ר הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶת־הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים יְרָא֙ וְאֶת־מִצְוֺתָ֣יו שְׁמ֔וֹר כִּי־זֶ֖ה כׇּל־הָאָדָֽם׃ יַעְלְז֣וּ חֲסִידִ֣ים בְּכָב֑וֹד יְ֝רַנְּנ֗וּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָֽם׃

parts.text: שָׁם תְּהֵא מְנַת וּמְחִיצַת וִישִׁיבַת נֶפֶשׁ הַשֵּׁם הַטּוֹב הַמְרוּחָם
דְּאִתְפְּטָר מִן עַלְמָא הָדֵין כִּרְעוּת אֱלָהָא מָארֵי שְׁמַיָּא וְאַרְעָא. מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים בְּרַחֲמָיו יְרַחֵם עָלָיו,
וְיָחוֹס וְיַחְמוֹל עָלָיו. מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמּלָכִים בְּרַחֲמָיו יַסְתִּירֵהוּ בְּצֵל כְּנָפָיו וּבְסֵתֶר אָהֳלוֹ לַחֲזוֹת בְּנוֹעַם יְהֹוָה וּלְבַקֵּר בְּהֵיכָלוֹ,
וְיָשִׂים כָּבוֹד מְנוּחָתוֹ. יְהֹוָה הוּא נַחֲלָתוֹ,
וְיִלָּוֶה אֵלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם וְעַל מִשְׁכָּבוֹ יִהְיֶה שָׁלוֹם,
כְּדִכְתִיב: יָב֣וֹא שָׁל֔וֹם יָנ֖וּחוּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם הֹלֵ֖ךְ נְכֹחֽוֹ׃ הוּא וְכָל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל הַשּׁוֹכְבִים עִמּוֹ בִּכְלַל הָרַחֲמִים וְהַסְּלִיחוֹת,

segs.en: Laying to Rest for a Woman
segs.text: השכבה לאשה

segs.en: Some have the custom to say:
segs.text: <small>יש נוהגים לומר</small>

אֵֽשֶׁת־חַ֭יִל מִ֣י יִמְצָ֑א וְרָחֹ֖ק מִפְּנִינִ֣ים מִכְרָֽהּ׃ שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭חֵן וְהֶ֣בֶל הַיֹּ֑פִי אִשָּׁ֥ה יִרְאַת־יְ֝הֹוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תִתְהַלָּֽל׃ תְּנוּ־לָ֭הּ מִפְּרִ֣י יָדֶ֑יהָ וִיהַלְל֖וּהָ בַשְּׁעָרִ֣ים מַֽעֲשֶֽׂיהָ׃

parts.text: הוּא יָחוּס וְיַחְמוֹל וִירַחֵם עַל נֶפֶשׁ רוּחַ וּנְשָׁמָה שֶׁל

segs.en: For a great and important woman, some say:
segs.text: <small>לאשה גדולה וחשובה יש אומרים</small>

אֵֽשֶׁת־חַ֭יִל מִ֣י יִמְצָ֑א וְרָחֹ֖ק מִפְּנִינִ֣ים מִכְרָֽהּ׃ שֶׁ֣קֶר הַ֭חֵן וְהֶ֣בֶל הַיֹּ֑פִי אִשָּׁ֥ה יִרְאַת־יְ֝הֹוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תִתְהַלָּֽל׃ תְּנוּ־לָ֭הּ מִפְּרִ֣י יָדֶ֑יהָ וִיהַלְל֖וּהָ בַשְּׁעָרִ֣ים מַֽעֲשֶֽׂיהָ׃

parts.text: רַחֲמָנָא דְּרַחֲמָנוּתָא דִי לֵיהּ הִיא וּבְמֵימְרֵיהּ אִתְבְּרִיאוּ עָֽלְמַיָּא עַלְמָא הָדֵין וְעַלְמָא דְּאָתֵי וּגְנַז בֵּיהּ צַדְקָנִיּוֹת וְחַסְדָּנִיּוֹת דְּעַבְדָן רְעוּתֵיהּ וּבְמֵימְרֵיהּ וּבִיקָרֵיהּ וּבְתוּקְפֵיהּ יֵאמַר לְמֵיעַל קֳדָמוֹהִי דּוּכְרָן נֶפֶשׁ הָאִשָּׁה הַכְּבֻדָּה וְהַצְּנוּעָה וְהַנִּכְבֶּדֶת מָרַת
דְּאִתְפְּטָרַת מִן עַלְמָא הָדֵין כִּרְעוּת אֱלָהָא מָארֵי שְׁמַיָּא וְאַרְעָא. הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּרַחֲמָיו יָחוֹס וְיַחְמוֹל עָלֶיהָ,
וְיִלָּוֶה אֵלֶיהָ הַשָּׁלוֹם וְעַל מִשְׁכָּבָה יִהְיֶה שָׁלוֹם,
כְּדִכְתִיב: יָב֣וֹא שָׁל֔וֹם יָנ֖וּחוּ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָ֑ם הֹלֵ֖ךְ נְכֹחֽוֹ׃ הִיא וְכָל־בְּנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל הַשּׁוֹכְבוֹת עִמָּהּ בִּכְלַל הָרַחֲמִים וְהַסְּלִיחוֹת,

segs.text: Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, the true Judge.

“You are righteous, Hashem, and Your judgments are upright.” “Hashem is righteous in all His ways and faithful in all His deeds.” “Your righteousness is everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth.” “The judgments of Hashem are true, altogether righteous.” “Where the word of the King rules, who can say to Him, ‘What are You doing?’ ” “He is unique, and who can turn Him back? What His soul desires, that He does.” “Small and great are there alike, and the servant is free of his master.” “Behold, He does not trust His servants, and He charges His angels with folly.” “How much more those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed like the moth!” “The Rock, His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice; a God of faithfulness and without iniquity, righteous and upright is He.” True Judge, Judge of righteousness and truth. Blessed is the true Judge, for all His judgments are righteous and true. He who has compassion on all His creatures will have pity, show compassion and have mercy on the soul, spirit and breath of [name]. The spirit of Hashem will give him (for a woman: her) rest in the Garden of Eden.

“He will swallow up death forever, and Hashem God will wipe away tears from all faces; and the disgrace of His people He will remove from all the earth, for Hashem has spoken.” “Your dead shall live; my corpses shall rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for Your dew is a dew of lights, and the earth will bring the shades to life.” “And He, being compassionate, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; He often turns back His anger and does not stir up all His wrath.” “Hashem, save! May the King answer us on the day we call.”
May you be comforted from Heaven.

A psalm of David. Hashem, who may dwell in Your tent? Who may live on Your holy mountain? One who walks blamelessly and does what is right, and speaks truth in his heart; who has no slander on his tongue, has done no evil to his fellow, and has not taken up a reproach against his relative; in whose eyes a contemptible person is despised, but who honors those who fear Hashem; who swears to his own hurt and does not change; who does not lend his money at interest and takes no bribe against the innocent. One who does these things shall never be shaken.
A Michtam of David. Preserve me, God, for I take refuge in You. I said to Hashem, “You are my Lord; I have no good beyond You.” As for the holy ones who are in the land, and the noble ones, all my delight is in them. Their sorrows multiply who hasten after another god; I will not pour out their libations of blood, nor take their names upon my lips. Hashem is the portion of my inheritance and my cup; You support my lot. The lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; indeed, my inheritance is lovely to me. I bless Hashem who has counseled me; even at night my conscience instructs me. I have set Hashem before me always; because He is at my right hand, I shall not be shaken. Therefore my heart rejoices and my glory exults; my flesh too will dwell in safety. For You will not abandon my soul to the grave; You will not let Your faithful one see the pit. You make known to me the path of life; in Your presence is fullness of joy, at Your right hand are delights for evermore.

Give us, and let us bless the exalted, holy King.
[The King of] Heaven.
With the permission of the exalted, holy King (on Shabbat: and with the permission of the Shabbat queen) and with your permission,
let us bless (with ten: our God,) the Comforter of mourners, of whose food we have eaten.
Blessed be (with ten: our God,) the Comforter of mourners, of whose food we have eaten and by whose great goodness we live.
Blessed be (with ten: our God,) the Comforter of mourners, of whose food we have eaten and by whose great goodness we live.

Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, the God who nourishes us and the whole world with His goodness, with grace, with kindness, with relief and with abundant compassion. He gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness endures forever. And through His great goodness we have never lacked, and may we never lack, sustenance, forever and ever. For He is a God who nourishes and provides for all, and His table is set for all, and He has prepared nourishment and sustenance for all His creatures whom He created in His mercy and abundant kindness, as it is said: “You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing with favor.” Blessed are You, Hashem, who nourishes all.

We thank You, Hashem our God, for having given our ancestors a desirable, good and spacious land; a covenant and Torah, life and sustenance; for having brought us out of the land of Egypt and redeemed us from the house of bondage; for Your covenant that You sealed in our flesh; for Your Torah that You taught us; for Your laws of favor that You made known to us; and for the life and sustenance with which You nourish and provide for us.

For everything, Hashem our God, we thank You and bless Your name, as it is said: “You shall eat and be satisfied, and bless Hashem your God for the good land that He has given you.” Blessed are You, Hashem, for the land and for the sustenance.

Have mercy, Hashem our God, on us and on Israel Your people, on Jerusalem Your city, on Mount Zion, the dwelling place of Your glory, on Your sanctuary, Your dwelling place and Your inner chamber, and on the great and holy House that is called by Your name. Our Father, tend us, feed us, nourish us, sustain us, and give us relief; give us relief speedily from all our troubles. And please, Hashem our God, do not make us dependent on gifts of flesh and blood, nor on their loans, but only on Your full, open, rich and generous hand, so that we are not ashamed in this world nor humiliated in the world to come. And restore the kingdom of the house of David, Your anointed, to its place, speedily in our days.

Console, Hashem our God, the mourners of Zion and the mourners of Jerusalem and the mourners who grieve in this mourning; comfort them from their grief and gladden them from their sorrow, as it is said: “As a man whom his mother comforts, so will I comfort you, and in Jerusalem you shall be comforted.” Blessed are You, Hashem, who comforts Zion by the rebuilding of Jerusalem. Amen. In our lifetime may the city of Zion be built, and the service be established in Jerusalem.

Blessed are You, Hashem, our God, King of the universe, the God, our Father, our King, our Mighty One, our Redeemer, our Holy One, the Holy One of Jacob; the King, the living, the good, who does good; the God of truth, Judge in righteousness, who takes souls, who rules over His world to do as He wills. We are His people and His servants, and for everything we are obliged to thank Him and bless Him. He who closes breaches, may He close this breach from us and from His people Israel, with compassion.
Amen.
He who makes peace in His heights, may He in His compassion make peace for us and for all His people Israel, and say: Amen.
He who has compassion on all His creatures will have pity, show compassion and have mercy on the soul, spirit and breath of [name]; the spirit of Hashem will give him rest in the Garden of Eden.

“But wisdom, where can it be found? And where is the place of understanding?” “Happy is the person who finds wisdom, the person who attains understanding.” “How abundant is Your goodness that You have stored up for those who fear You, that You have done for those who take refuge in You, before the children of men.” “How precious is Your kindness, God! The children of men take refuge in the shadow of Your wings. They are sated with the abundance of Your house, and You give them to drink from the stream of Your delights.” “A good name is better than fine oil, and the day of death than the day of one’s birth.” “The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole of man.” “Let the devout exult in glory; let them sing for joy upon their beds.”

[May there be] fitting rest in the high abode, in the rank of the holy and pure, who shine and radiate like the brilliance of the firmament; with the strengthening of the bones, atonement for guilt, removal of transgression, nearness of deliverance, and mercy and grace from before Him who dwells in the heavenly abode; and a good portion in the life of the world to come. There shall be the portion, the company and the dwelling of the soul of the one of good name, who has been shown mercy, [name]; the spirit of Hashem will give him rest in the Garden of Eden; who has departed from this world according to the will of God, Master of heaven and earth. May the King, King of kings, in His mercy have compassion on him, and spare him and pity him. May the King, King of kings, in His mercy hide him in the shelter of His wings and in the secret place of His tent, to behold the pleasantness of Hashem and to visit in His Sanctuary; and at the end of days may He raise him up, and give him to drink from the stream of His delights; may He bind his soul in the bond of life and place honor in his resting place. Hashem is his inheritance; and may peace accompany him, and on his resting place may there be peace, as it is written: “Peace shall come; they shall rest on their beds, each who walked in his uprightness.” He and all Israel who lie with him, in the company of mercy and forgiveness. And so may it be His will, and let us say: Amen.

“A woman of valor, who can find? Her worth is far beyond pearls. Charm is deceptive and beauty is vain; a woman who fears Hashem, she shall be praised. Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her deeds praise her in the gates.”
He who has compassion on all His creatures will have pity, show compassion and have mercy on the soul, spirit and breath of [name]; the spirit of Hashem will give her rest in the Garden of Eden.

“A woman of valor, who can find? Her worth is far beyond pearls. Charm is deceptive and beauty is vain; a woman who fears Hashem, she shall be praised. Give her of the fruit of her hands, and let her deeds praise her in the gates.”

Merciful One, whose is mercy, by whose word the worlds were created, this world and the world to come, who has stored up in it the righteous and kind deeds of those who do His will: by His word, by His glory and by His might, may the remembrance of the soul of the esteemed, modest and honored woman, Mrs. [name], come before Him; the spirit of Hashem will give her rest in the Garden of Eden; who has departed from this world according to the will of God, Master of heaven and earth. May the King in His mercy spare her and have compassion on her; and may peace accompany her, and on her resting place may there be peace, as it is written: “Peace shall come; they shall rest on their beds, each who walked in his uprightness.” She and all the daughters of Israel who lie with her, in the company of mercy and forgiveness. And so may it be His will, and let us say: Amen.

parts.text: וַיְחַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֖י יְהֹוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָמָ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ יֶחֱרֶ֤ה אַפְּךָ֙ בְּעַמֶּ֔ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵ֙אתָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּכֹ֥חַ גָּד֖וֹל וּבְיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃ לָ֩מָּה֩ יֹאמְר֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר בְּרָעָ֤ה הֽוֹצִיאָם֙ לַהֲרֹ֤ג אֹתָם֙ בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּ֨לְכַלֹּתָ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה שׁ֚וּב מֵחֲר֣וֹן אַפֶּ֔ךָ וְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל־הָרָעָ֖ה לְעַמֶּֽךָ׃ זְכֹ֡ר לְאַבְרָהָם֩ לְיִצְחָ֨ק וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתָּ לָהֶם֮ בָּךְ֒ וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַרְבֶּה֙ אֶֽת־זַרְעֲכֶ֔ם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְכׇל־הָאָ֨רֶץ הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶתֵּן֙ לְזַרְעֲכֶ֔ם וְנָחֲל֖וּ לְעֹלָֽם׃ וַיִּנָּ֖חֶם יְהֹוָ֑ה עַל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְעַמּֽוֹ׃

וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהֹוָה֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה פְּסׇל־לְךָ֛ שְׁנֵֽי־לֻחֹ֥ת אֲבָנִ֖ים כָּרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים וְכָתַבְתִּי֙ עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֔ת אֶ֨ת־הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֛וּ עַל־הַלֻּחֹ֥ת הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שִׁבַּֽרְתָּ׃ וֶהְיֵ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן לַבֹּ֑קֶר וְעָלִ֤יתָ בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ אֶל־הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י וְנִצַּבְתָּ֥ לִ֛י שָׁ֖ם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָהָֽר׃ וְאִישׁ֙ לֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ וְגַם־אִ֥ישׁ אַל־יֵרָ֖א בְּכׇל־הָהָ֑ר גַּם־הַצֹּ֤אן וְהַבָּקָר֙ אַל־יִרְע֔וּ אֶל־מ֖וּל הָהָ֥ר הַהֽוּא׃

וַיִּפְסֹ֡ל שְׁנֵֽי־לֻחֹ֨ת אֲבָנִ֜ים כָּרִאשֹׁנִ֗ים וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם מֹשֶׁ֤ה בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ וַיַּ֙עַל֙ אֶל־הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהֹוָ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָד֔וֹ שְׁנֵ֖י לֻחֹ֥ת אֲבָנִֽים׃ וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהֹוָה֙ בֶּֽעָנָ֔ן וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב עִמּ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְשֵׁ֖ם יְהֹוָֽה׃ וַיַּעֲבֹ֨ר יְהֹוָ֥ה ׀ עַל־פָּנָיו֮ וַיִּקְרָא֒ יְהֹוָ֣ה ׀ יְהֹוָ֔ה אֵ֥ל רַח֖וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַפַּ֖יִם וְרַב־חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׃ <big>נֹ</big>צֵ֥ר‏ חֶ֙סֶד֙ לָאֲלָפִ֔ים נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֛ן וָפֶ֖שַׁע וְחַטָּאָ֑ה וְנַקֵּה֙ לֹ֣א יְנַקֶּ֔ה פֹּקֵ֣ד ׀ עֲוֺ֣ן אָב֗וֹת עַל־בָּנִים֙ וְעַל־בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים עַל־שִׁלֵּשִׁ֖ים וְעַל־רִבֵּעִֽים׃ וַיְמַהֵ֖ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּקֹּ֥ד אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃ וַיֹּ֡אמֶר אִם־נָא֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲדֹנָ֔י יֵֽלֶךְ־נָ֥א אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּקִרְבֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֤י עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֙רֶף֙ ה֔וּא וְסָלַחְתָּ֛ לַעֲוֺנֵ֥נוּ וּלְחַטָּאתֵ֖נוּ וּנְחַלְתָּֽנוּ׃ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִי֮ כֹּרֵ֣ת בְּרִית֒ נֶ֤גֶד כׇּֽל־עַמְּךָ֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה נִפְלָאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־נִבְרְא֥וּ בְכׇל־הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבְכׇל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְרָאָ֣ה כׇל־הָ֠עָ֠ם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֨ה בְקִרְבּ֜וֹ אֶת־מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יְהֹוָה֙ כִּֽי־נוֹרָ֣א ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י עֹשֶׂ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

segs.text:
Moses entreated Hashem his God, and said, “Why, Hashem, does Your anger burn against Your people, whom You brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand? Why should the Egyptians say, ‘It was with evil intent that He brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them from the face of the earth’? Turn from Your burning anger and relent from doing harm to Your people. Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, Your servants, to whom You swore by Your very self and said to them, ‘I will multiply your descendants like the stars of heaven, and all this land of which I have spoken I will give to your descendants, and they shall inherit it forever.’” And Hashem relented from the harm that He had spoken of doing to His people.
Hashem said to Moses, “Carve for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke. Be ready by morning, and go up in the morning to Mount Sinai and present yourself to Me there on the top of the mountain. No one shall go up with you, and let no one be seen anywhere on the mountain; even the flocks and herds shall not graze at the foot of that mountain.”
He carved two stone tablets like the first ones, and Moses rose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai, as Hashem had commanded him, taking in his hand the two stone tablets. Hashem descended in the cloud and stood with him there, and called out the name of Hashem. Hashem passed before him and proclaimed: “Hashem, Hashem, God, compassionate and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in kindness and truth, extending kindness to the thousandth generation, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and pardoning; yet He does not leave the guilty unpunished, visiting the iniquity of parents upon children and children’s children, to the third and fourth generations.” Moses hurried and bowed his head to the ground and prostrated himself. He said, “If I have found favor in Your eyes, my Lord, let my Lord go in our midst, for it is a stiff-necked people; forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your own.” He said, “Behold, I make a covenant: before all your people I will perform wonders such as have not been created in all the earth or in any nation; and all the people among whom you live shall see the work of Hashem, for it is awesome, what I will do with you.”
